# Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity

{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove sharp spacetime Penrose inequalities for invariant ADM mass and minimum enclosing area in three and four spatial dimensions. Under their respective designated-end conventions, the neutral numerical results allow arbitrary second fundamental form, nonzero momentum, disconnected weakly future trapped boundary, and finitely many ends. Under the stated horizon hypotheses, equality for the neutral inequalities reconstructs the original exterior data as spacelike slices of Schwarzschild spacetime in three dimensions and Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime in four; the four-dimensional equality theorem concerns a connected, one-ended exterior. We also prove a three-dimensional electric–magnetic charged upper-area inequality for one-ended data with nonzero momentum, with separate purely electric rest-frame corollaries allowing finitely many ends. Finally, for each fixed transverse-traceless seed and prescribed decaying solution branch, we prove a local Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter inequality.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove sharp spacetime Penrose inequalities for invariant ADM mass and minimum enclosing area in three and four spatial dimensions. Under their respective designated-end conventions, the neutral numerical results allow arbitrary second fundamental form, nonzero momentum, disconnected weakly future trapped boundary, and finitely many ends. Under the stated horizon hypotheses, equality for the neutral inequalities reconstructs the original exterior data as spacelike slices of Schwarzschild spacetime in three dimensions and Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime in four; the four-dimensional equality theorem concerns a connected, one-ended exterior. We also prove a three-dimensional electric–magnetic charged upper-area inequality for one-ended data with nonzero momentum, with separate purely electric rest-frame corollaries allowing finitely many ends. Finally, for each fixed transverse-traceless seed and prescribed decaying solution branch, we prove a local Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter inequality.

- **C1** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-intro-exterior-inequality)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ be an exterior as in Definition <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-class">1</a>. Assume Equations <a href="#n3:intro:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:constraints">[n3:intro:constraints]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:decay">[n3:intro:decay]</a>, integrability of $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$, and the finite ADM limits <a href="#n3:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:energy">[n3:intro:energy]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:momentum">[n3:intro:momentum]</a>. Orient $\partial\Omega$ by the normal into $\Omega$, and suppose $\theta_+(\partial\Omega)\le0$. If $E>\|P\|_\delta$, then $$\label{n3:intro:penrose} \sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2} \ge \sqrt{\frac{a_g(\partial\Omega)}{16\pi}}.$$ No extension of the data across $\partial\Omega$ is required.
  - Explanation: The invariant mass bounds the full minimum enclosing area under the stated one-ended exterior assumptions.
- **C2** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-rest-reduction)): Let $(N,g,K)$ satisfy the exterior hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">2</a>, including $\theta_+\le0$ on its smooth compact boundary, and let $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}>0$. There is a sequence of smooth exterior data $(g_j,K_j)$ on $N$ with the following properties:* 1. *$\mu_j>\|J_j\|_{g_j}$ everywhere and $\theta_{+,j}<0$ on $B$. The constraint densities are integrable. On the end their DEC margin is bounded below by $c_jr^{-3-\delta}$ for some $c_j>0$ and one fixed $0<\delta<1$.* 2. *$K_j$ is compactly supported, and in a rest chart $g_j-\delta=O_k(r^{-1})$ and $R_{g_j}=O_k(r^{-3-\delta})$ for every $k$. In particular $\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{g_j}=O(r^{-3})$ there. Their ADM momentum is zero.* 3. *$(g_j,K_j)\to(g,K)$ smoothly on every fixed compact subset up to the boundary, their ADM energies satisfy $E_j\to m$, and $a_{g_j}(B)\to a_g(B)$.* *Consequently it suffices to prove the energy/enclosing-area inequality for the class in <span class="upright">(i)</span>–<span class="upright">(ii)</span> in order to prove Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">2</a> in its stated class.
  - Explanation: Strict exterior approximations reduce the invariant-mass problem to a zero-momentum energy inequality while preserving the enclosing infimum in the limit.
- **C3** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-existence-deformation)): For the prepared domain of Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">19</a> and every sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$, there is an integer $n_0\ge4$ and, for each $n\ge n_0$, a radius $R_{\min}(n)$, with $R_{\min}(n)\to\infty$, such that the original deformation system has a smooth solution on every $\Omega_R$ with $R\ge R_{\min}(n)$. It satisfies $t>-\epsilon$ on the closure. At fixed $n$, these solutions have the local bounds of Proposition <a href="#n3:existence:classical-bounds" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:existence:classical-bounds">36</a>, uniformly as $R\to\infty$. In particular, any sequence $R_j\to\infty$ of such radii has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of $\overline\Omega$ to a solution of the original equations with $t\ge-\epsilon$.
  - Explanation: The prepared coupled deformation has smooth solutions on sufficiently large truncations and subsequential limits at fixed parameters.
- **C4** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-limit-energy)): The reduced data satisfy $$E\ge\sqrt{\frac{A_*}{16\pi}}.$$ Consequently Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">2</a> holds in its entire stated exterior class.
  - Explanation: The reduced energy inequality completes the neutral exterior comparison.
- **C5** (bound, [source](#stmt-bridge-intro-global-penrose)): For the complete initial data just specified, every chosen end and every admissible boundary satisfy $$\label{bridge:intro:global-inequality} E>\|P\|_\delta,\qquad \sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2} \ge \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{16\pi}}.$$ Here $(E,P)$ is the ADM vector of the chosen end. The assertion allows finitely many ends and disconnected admissible boundaries.
  - Explanation: The designated-end complete-data formulation permits finitely many ends and disconnected admissible boundaries.
- **C6** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bridge-bridge-timelike)): Let $(N,g,K)$ satisfy all the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">2</a> except the assumption $E>\|P\|_\delta$. Then $E>\|P\|_\delta$ and the conclusion of that theorem holds. No extension of the data across the compact boundary $B$ is required.
  - Explanation: The neutral exterior conclusion holds without imposing timelikeness as an additional assumption.
- **C7** (classification, [source](#stmt-n3-intro-rigidity)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end assume $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$, $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$, with $q>1/2$, and existing finite ADM flux limits. Assume that $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$ are integrable and that $\mu\geq\|J\|_g$ everywhere.* *Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union $$S=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{\ell}S_i,\qquad 1\leq\ell<\infty,$$ of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that $\partial M_{\mathrm{ext}}=S$, that $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$:* 1. *every $S_i$ is a future MOTS, so $H_{S_i}+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{S_i}K=0$;* 2. *$S$ is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition <a href="#n3:rigidity:partial-outermostness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:rigidity:partial-outermostness">47</a>;* 3. *every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least $A=\|S\|_g=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\|S_i\|_g>0$.* *Let $(E,P)$ be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If $$\label{n3:intro:equality} E>\|P\|_\delta,\qquad m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}=\sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}},$$ then $\ell=1$ and $S$ is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$, inducing $g$ and the given $K$ for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of $S$ is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to $S$, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.
  - Explanation: Exact equality with the specified horizon and partial-coincidence outermostness assumptions forces one spherical boundary and reconstructs the original Schwarzschild exterior slice.
- **C8** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-rigidity-finite-strictness)): Under the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:rigidity">48</a>, retain $E>\|P\|_\delta$ but do not assume its equality in mass and area. If $\ell\geq2$, then $$\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}>\sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}.$$
  - Explanation: Disconnected horizons in the specified rigidity class satisfy strict mass-area inequality.
- **C9** (classification, [source](#stmt-n3-static-classification)): Let the original exterior satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:rigidity">48</a>, and let $u,X$ be the fields supplied by Proposition <a href="#n3:variation:adjoint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:variation:adjoint">50</a>. Then the number of boundary components is $\ell=1$, and that component is diffeomorphic to $S^2$. Moreover, $$N:=u^2-\|X\|_g^2>0 \qquad\text{on }\operatorname{int}M_{\mathrm{ext}}.$$ The metric and function $$h=g+N^{-1}X^\flat\otimes X^\flat,\qquad \lambda=\sqrt N$$ form the Schwarzschild static base of mass $m$, with its horizon boundary attached in the regular base coordinates described below. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the original $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ into maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$ whose induced metric and future second fundamental form are $g,K$. Its boundary is a cross-section of the future horizon if $u\|_S>0$, and the bifurcation sphere if $u\|_S=0$. The embedding extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through $S$, and its chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity.
  - Explanation: The causal stationary field determines the Schwarzschild static base and the original smooth hypersurface.
- **C10** (bound, [source](#stmt-ch-intro-main)): Let $(N,g,K,\mathcal E,\mathcal B)$ be a charged exterior in the sense of Definition <a href="#ch:pre:charged-exterior" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ch:pre:charged-exterior">70</a>, with inner boundary $S$, ADM energy and momentum $(E,P)$, and total charges $(Q_E,Q_B)$. Then $E>\|P\|$. Setting $$m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|^2},\qquad Q=\sqrt{Q_E^2+Q_B^2},\qquad r=\sqrt{a_g(S)/(4\pi)},$$ we have $$m\ge Q,\qquad r\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}.$$
  - Explanation: The charged one-ended theorem bounds area radius from above and mass from below by total charge; electromagnetic momentum is included in the matter hypothesis.
- **C11** (construction, [source](#stmt-ch-rest-reduction)): For a charged exterior as in Definition <a href="#ch:pre:charged-exterior" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ch:pre:charged-exterior">70</a>, $E>\|P\|$ and $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}>0$. There are smooth data $(g_j,K_j)$ on the same exterior, with the same flux forms, satisfying the following properties.* 1. *The physical matter condition is strict everywhere, the original boundary $S$ has $\theta_{+,j}<0$, and the constraint densities remain integrable. For one fixed $0<\delta<1$ the matter margin satisfies $$M_{0,j}=8\pi(\mu_{m,j}-\|J_{m,j}\|_{g_j}) \ge c_j r_y^{-3-\delta}\quad\hbox{far out},\qquad c_j>0.$$* 2. *In a rest chart $y$, $K_j$ is compactly supported and $$g_j-\delta_{\mathrm{eucl}}=O_k(r_y^{-1}),\qquad R_{g_j}=O_k(r_y^{-3-\delta})\quad\hbox{for every }k.$$ The fields have the required $O_1(r_y^{-2})$ decay. In particular the ADM momentum is zero and $\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{g_j}=O(r_y^{-3})$.* 3. *Smooth convergence holds on every compact set, including at $S$, and $$\label{ch:rest:limits} E_j\longrightarrow m,\qquad a_{g_j}(S)\longrightarrow a_g(S),\qquad (Q_{E,j},Q_{B,j})=(Q_E,Q_B).$$ Moreover $g_j\ge(1-\varepsilon_j)g$ globally for some $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$.
  - Explanation: Strict rest approximations preserve the two electromagnetic charges while controlling mass and full enclosing area.
- **C12** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-chext-cor-charged-electric-rest)): Let $(\Omega^3,g,K,\mathcal E)$ be smooth and orientable, with $\Omega$ connected and complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one asymptotically flat end. The boundary may have finitely many components. Define $$16\pi\mu=R_g+(\operatorname{tr}_gK)^2-\|K\|_g^2, \qquad 8\pi J=\operatorname{div}_g \bigl(K-(\operatorname{tr}_gK)g\bigr).$$ Assume that $\mu,\|J\|_g$ are integrable, that the ADM limits exist, and that, for some $q>1/2$, the end satisfies $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad \mathcal E=O_1(r^{-2}).$$ There is no magnetic field. Suppose throughout $\Omega$ that $$\label{chext:eq:charged-electric-matter-dec} \operatorname{div}_g\mathcal E=0, \qquad \mu-\frac{\|\mathcal E\|_g^2}{8\pi}\ge \|J\|_g,$$ and on $S$, with normal into $\Omega$, that $H+\operatorname{tr}_S K\le0$. Let $a=a_g(S)$ be the minimum enclosing area over all smooth filled cuts of the entire boundary, and put $$r_a=\sqrt{\frac{a}{4\pi}},\qquad Q=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S \langle\mathcal E,\nu\rangle_g\,dA_g.$$ If the ADM momentum vanishes and $r_a\ge \|Q\|$, then the ADM energy $m$ is positive and $$\label{chext:eq:charged-electric-rest-bound} m\ge\frac12\left(r_a+\frac{Q^2}{r_a}\right).$$
  - Explanation: The purely electric rest-frame lower-mass formula requires the stated area-radius branch.
- **C13** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-chext-cor-charged-electric-boundary-area)): Under the hypotheses of Corollary <a href="#chext:cor:charged-electric-rest" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="chext:cor:charged-electric-rest">94</a>, suppose that every filled enclosing cut of the whole boundary has area at least $A=\operatorname{Area}_g(S)$. If $A\ge4\pi Q^2$, then $$m\ge\sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}+Q^2\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{A}}.$$ In particular this applies to maximal purely electric source-free electrovacuum data with such a boundary and zero ADM momentum.
  - Explanation: Outer area-minimization identifies the enclosing infimum with boundary area under the stated charged branch condition.
- **C14** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-chext-thm-charged-electric-finite-ends)): Let $(\Omega^3,g,K,\mathcal E)$ be smooth, connected and orientable, complete with its compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and have the finitely many asymptotically flat ends just described. Assume <a href="#chext:eq:charged-electric-matter-dec" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="chext:eq:charged-electric-matter-dec">[chext:eq:charged-electric-matter-dec]</a> everywhere, integrable $\mu,\|J\|_g$, and $H+\operatorname{tr}_S K\le0$ with the normal into $\Omega$ on every component of $S$. Assume the end falloff of Corollary <a href="#chext:cor:charged-electric-rest" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="chext:cor:charged-electric-rest">94</a> on each end, with a common $q>1/2$, and finite ADM limits at the designated end. There is no magnetic field. Let $$Q_0=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S_R^0} \langle\mathcal E,\nu_R\rangle_g\,dA_g$$ be its conserved outward charge. Suppose its ADM momentum is zero and that $0<a_0$ and $r_0\ge\|Q_0\|$, with $a_0$ as in <a href="#chext:eq:charged-designated-area" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="chext:eq:charged-designated-area">[chext:eq:charged-designated-area]</a>. Then its ADM energy $m_0$ is positive and $$\label{chext:eq:charged-finite-ends-bound} m_0\ge\frac12\left(r_0+\frac{Q_0^2}{r_0}\right).$$ No momentum condition is imposed at the other ends.
  - Explanation: The designated-end purely electric rest-frame statement has its own cut convention and finitely-many-ends hypotheses.
- **C15** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-thm-main)): Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth and connected, with $M$ orientable, $K$ an arbitrary smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $S=\partial M$ nonempty, compact, and smooth. Suppose $g$ is complete as a metric space with $S$ included. Outside a compact set let $M$ have finitely many, and at least one, ends diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb R^4$. Assume $$\mu\ge\|J\|_g,\qquad \mu,\|J\|_g\in L^1(M,\,\mathrm dV_g),$$ and, on every end for a common $q>1$, $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ with finite energy and momentum limits <a href="#four:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:intro:energy">[four:intro:energy]</a>–<a href="#four:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:intro:momentum">[four:intro:momentum]</a>. On every component of $S$ assume $\Theta_K\le0$, with normal into $M$.* *Then for each end $e$, $$\label{four:intro:main} E_e\ge \sqrt{\|P_e\|_\delta^2+ \frac14\left(\frac{A_e(S)}{\omega}\right)^{4/3}}.$$ In particular $E_e>\|P_e\|_\delta$, and the invariant mass satisfies $$\label{four:intro:mass} \sqrt{E_e^2-\|P_e\|_\delta^2} \ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_e(S)}{\omega}\right)^{2/3}.$$
  - Explanation: The neutral inequality in four spatial dimensions allows arbitrary second fundamental form and finitely many ends; timelikeness is a conclusion.
- **C16** (classification, [source](#stmt-rig4-thm-rigidity)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ belong to Definition <a href="#rig4:def:horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rig4:def:horizon">99</a>, and put $m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}$. Then $$\label{rig4:eq:intro-equality} m=\frac12\left(\frac A\omega\right)^{2/3}$$ if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including $S$, into the regular maximal extension of $\overline g_m$. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, the chosen end approaches its spatial infinity, and $S$ maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The pullback of the spacetime metric is $g$; for a consistent future unit normal $n$, the second fundamental form is precisely the original tensor $K$, with the convention $$\label{rig4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form} K(U,V)=\overline g_m(\overline\nabla_U n,V).$$ Both the embedding and the normal extend smoothly to $S$ in horizon-regular coordinates.* *Equivalently, every such Schwarzschild–Tangherlini hypersurface in $\overline g_{M_0}$ satisfying Definition <a href="#rig4:def:horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rig4:def:horizon">99</a> and the prescribed asymptotic hypotheses has invariant ADM mass $M_0$, horizon area $\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$, and equality in Theorem <a href="#four:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:thm:main">98</a>.
  - Explanation: In the connected one-ended horizon class, equality is equivalent to smooth realization of the original data in the regular Tangherlini extension.
- **C17** (construction, [source](#stmt-four-prop-existence)): Fix the prepared geometry and $0<\epsilon<1$. For every sufficiently large $n$ and every allowed $R$, system <a href="#four:eq:system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:eq:system">[four:eq:system]</a> has a smooth solution on $\overline\Omega_R$ with $t>-\epsilon$. For each such fixed $n$ there is a sequence $R\to\infty$ whose solutions converge smoothly on compact subsets up to $B$ to a solution on $\overline\Omega$ with $t\ge-\epsilon$. This solution satisfies the prescribed inner boundary conditions, the height interval <a href="#four:eq:height-interval" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:eq:height-interval">[four:eq:height-interval]</a>, and the weighted trace and flux estimates of Lemma <a href="#four:lem:weighted-trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:lem:weighted-trace">128</a>.
  - Explanation: The four-dimensional coupled system has smooth finite-truncation solutions and exhaustion limits in the specified prepared regime.
- **C18** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-thm-prepared-energy)): Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth, connected, and orientable, complete with a nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat. Let $K$ be a smooth compactly supported symmetric covariant tensor. Suppose, with a smooth positive function $r$ equal to the coordinate radius on the end, constants $c_0>0$ and $0<\delta_1<1$, that $$\mu-\|J\|_g\ge c_0r^{-4-\delta_1}\quad\hbox{on }M, \qquad H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK<0\quad\hbox{on every component of }S,$$ where the boundary normal points into $M$. Suppose on the end that $$g-\delta=O_k(r^{-2})\quad\hbox{for every integer }k\ge0, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g=O(r^{-4-\delta_1}),$$ and that the ADM energy $E_g$ is finite in the stated normalization. Let $A_*$ be the infimum of the total $g$-three-volume of the entire intrinsic boundaries of connected closed smooth outer domains containing the distant end, with interiors disjoint from $S$, including disconnected cuts and frontier coincident with $S$. Then $$\label{four:ex:prepared-inequality} E_g\ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_*}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}.$$
  - Explanation: The prepared energy estimate follows from energy and area comparison with the Riemannian inequality.
- **C19** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-ads-thm-main)): For every background, fixed TT seed, and solution branch satisfying <a href="#ads:eq:background" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ads:eq:background">[ads:eq:background]</a>–<a href="#ads:eq:branch" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ads:eq:branch">[ads:eq:branch]</a> and the mass assumptions above, there is $0<\epsilon_0\leq\epsilon_*$ such that $$m_{\mathrm{AH}}(\epsilon)\geq \sqrt{\frac{A_\epsilon}{16\pi}}\left(1+\frac{A_\epsilon}{4\pi}\right) \qquad(0\leq\epsilon<\epsilon_0).$$ For all sufficiently small positive $\epsilon$, equality holds if the seed is radial, and the inequality is strict otherwise.
  - Explanation: The local AdS inequality is seed- and branch-dependent; radial seeds give equality and other seeds give strict inequality on a sufficiently small positive interval.
- **C20** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-ads-cor-penrose)): In addition to the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#ads:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ads:thm:main">176</a>, suppose $q_{ss}\geq0$ on $S$. Assume, for every sufficiently small positive $\epsilon$, that no compact smooth embedded two-sided surface in the interior enclosing $S$ has $\theta_+\leq0$ everywhere, and that every smooth enclosing surface has area at least $A_\epsilon$. Disconnected enclosing competitors are allowed, and $S$ itself is allowed in the area infimum. Then the exact local Penrose inequality holds with $A_{\min}(S)=A_\epsilon$.
  - Explanation: Additional outermostness, area-minimization and boundary sign hypotheses identify prescribed area with enclosing infimum in the local AdS setting.
- **C21** (classification, [source](#stmt-ads-cor-kernel)): The kernel of $c_2$ is exactly $\mathcal K$, a four-dimensional real vector space. In particular, the nonzero degree-one directions are genuine quadratic null directions.
  - Explanation: The complete quadratic null space includes genuine nonradial degree-one directions, so quadratic vanishing alone does not imply radiality.
- **C22** (bound, [source](#stmt-ads-prop-quartic)): Suppose that $c_2[q]=0$. Write the representation furnished by Corollary <a href="#ads:cor:kernel" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ads:cor:kernel">191</a> as $$q=Q(v):=\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_{g_0}v-Bv,\qquad Lv=0, \qquad v=v_0(s)+v_1(s,x),$$ where $v_1$ has only degree-one spherical modes and $v$ decays at infinity. Then $$c_0[q]=c_1[q]=c_2[q]=c_3[q]=0, \qquad c_4[q]\geq 0.$$ If $v_1\not\equiv0$, then $c_4[q]>0$. In particular, in that case the actual deficit $\mathfrak D_q(\epsilon)$ is strictly positive for all sufficiently small positive $\epsilon$.
  - Explanation: The quartic coefficient resolves nontrivial degree-one directions in the quadratic kernel and gives strict positive deficit locally.
- **C23** (classification, [source](#stmt-ads-prop-radial)): Suppose the fixed TT seed $q$ is invariant under rotations of $S^2$. Every branch in Theorem <a href="#ads:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ads:thm:main">176</a> is radial for all sufficiently small $\epsilon$, and on that parameter interval $$m_{\mathrm{AH}}(\epsilon)=b_*(A_\epsilon).$$ This includes the zero seed, and requires no sign for $q_{ss}\|_S$.
  - Explanation: Radial fixed seeds yield radial actual solution branches and exact local equality without a boundary seed sign restriction.

          "source_id": "PM-260.3"
        }

          "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. Assume that $\\mu$ and $|J|_g$ are integrable and that $\\mu\\geq|J|_g$ everywhere.*\n\n*Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union $$S=\\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{\\ell}S_i,\\qquad 1\\leq\\ell<\\infty,$$ of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that $\\partial M_{\\mathrm{ext}}=S$, that $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$:*\n\n1.  *every $S_i$ is a future MOTS, so $H_{S_i}+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{S_i}K=0$;*\n\n2.  *$S$ is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition <a href=\"#n3:rigidity:partial-outermostness\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:rigidity:partial-outermostness\">47</a>;*\n\n3.  *every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least $A=|S|_g=\\sum_{i=1}^{\\ell}|S_i|_g>0$.*\n\n*Let $(E,P)$ be the ADM vector of the chosen end. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$, inducing $g$ and the given $K$ for a consistent future unit normal.         "anchor": "stmt-chext-cor-charged-electric-rest",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega^3,g,K,\\mathcal E)$ be smooth and orientable, with $\\Omega$ connected and complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one asymptotically flat end. The boundary may have finitely many components. Define $$16\\pi\\mu=R_g+(\\operatorname{tr}_gK)^2-|K|_g^2,\n \\qquad\n 8\\pi J=\\operatorname{div}_g\n       \\bigl(K-(\\operatorname{tr}_gK)g\\bigr).$$ Assume that $\\mu,|J|_g$ are integrable, that the ADM limits exist, and that, for some $q>1/2$, the end satisfies $$g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad\n K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\\qquad \\mathcal E=O_1(r^{-2}).$$ There is no magnetic field. Suppose throughout $\\Omega$ that $$\\label{chext:eq:charged-electric-matter-dec}\n \\operatorname{div}_g\\mathcal E=0,\n \\qquad\n \\mu-\\frac{|\\mathcal E|_g^2}{8\\pi}\\ge |J|_g,$$ and on $S$, with normal into $\\Omega$, that $H+\\operatorname{tr}_S K\\le0$. Let $a=a_g(S)$ be the minimum enclosing area over all smooth filled cuts of the entire boundary, and put $$r_a=\\sqrt{\\frac{a}{4\\pi}},\\qquad\n Q=\\frac1{4\\pi}\\int_S\n           \\langle\\mathcal E,\\nu\\rangle_g\\,dA_g.$$ If the ADM momentum vanishes and $r_a\\ge |Q|$, then the ADM energy $m$ is positive and $$\\label{chext:eq:charged-electric-rest-bound}\n m\\ge\\frac12\\left(r_a+\\frac{Q^2}{r_a}\\right).$$",

      },

      "exact_statement": "Let $(\\Omega^3,g,K,\\mathcal E)$ be smooth and orientable, with $\\Omega$ connected and complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one asymptotically flat end. The boundary may have finitely many components. Define $$16\\pi\\mu=R_g+(\\operatorname{tr}_gK)^2-|K|_g^2,\n \\qquad\n 8\\pi J=\\operatorname{div}_g\n       \\bigl(K-(\\operatorname{tr}_gK)g\\bigr).$$ Assume that $\\mu,|J|_g$ are integrable, that the ADM limits exist, and that, for some $q>1/2$, the end satisfies $$g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad\n K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\\qquad \\mathcal E=O_1(r^{-2}).$$ There is no magnetic field. Suppose throughout $\\Omega$ that $$\\label{chext:eq:charged-electric-matter-dec}\n \\operatorname{div}_g\\mathcal E=0,\n \\qquad\n \\mu-\\frac{|\\mathcal E|_g^2}{8\\pi}\\ge |J|_g,$$ and on $S$, with normal into $\\Omega$, that $H+\\operatorname{tr}_S K\\le0$. Let $a=a_g(S)$ be the minimum enclosing area over all smooth filled cuts of the entire boundary, and put $$r_a=\\sqrt{\\frac{a}{4\\pi}},\\qquad\n Q=\\frac1{4\\pi}\\int_S\n           \\langle\\mathcal E,\\nu\\rangle_g\\,dA_g.$$ If the ADM momentum vanishes and $r_a\\ge |Q|$, then the ADM energy $m$ is positive and $$\\label{chext:eq:charged-electric-rest-bound}\n m\\ge\\frac12\\left(r_a+\\frac{Q^2}{r_a}\\right).$$",
      "explanation": "The purely electric rest-frame lower-mass formula requires the stated area-radius branch.",

        "anchor": "stmt-four-thm-main",
        "exact_quote": "\n*Then for each end $e$, $$\\label{four:intro:main}\n E_e\\ge\n \\sqrt{|P_e|_\\delta^2+\n       \\frac14\\left(\\frac{A_e(S)}{\\omega}\\right)^{4/3}}.$$ In particular $E_e>|P_e|_\\delta$, and the invariant mass satisfies $$\\label{four:intro:mass}\n \\sqrt{E_e^2-|P_e|_\\delta^2}\n   \\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A_e(S)}{\\omega}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.3"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-four-thm-main",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth and connected, with $M$ orientable, $K$ an arbitrary smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $S=\\partial M$ nonempty, compact, and smooth. Outside a compact set let $M$ have finitely many, and at least one, ends diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\\mathbb R^4$. Assume $$\\mu\\ge|J|_g,\\qquad \\mu,|J|_g\\in L^1(M,\\,\\mathrm dV_g),$$ and, on every end for a common $q>1$, $$g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ with finite energy and momentum limits <a href=\"#four:intro:energy\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"four:intro:energy\">[four:intro:energy]</a>–<a href=\"#four:intro:momentum\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"four:intro:momentum\">[four:intro:momentum]</a>. On every component of $S$ assume $\\Theta_K\\le0$, with normal into $M$.*\n\n\n*Then for each end $e$, $$\\label{four:intro:main}\n E_e\\ge\n \\sqrt{|P_e|_\\delta^2+\n       \\frac14\\left(\\frac{A_e(S)}{\\omega}\\right)^{4/3}}.$$ In particular $E_e>|P_e|_\\delta$, and the invariant mass satisfies $$\\label{four:intro:mass}\n \\sqrt{E_e^2-|P_e|_\\delta^2}\n   \\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A_e(S)}{\\omega}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",
          "source_id": "PM-260.3"
        }

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-rig4-thm-rigidity",
        "exact_quote": "*Equivalently, every such Schwarzschild–Tangherlini hypersurface in $\\overline g_{M_0}$ satisfying Definition <a href=\"#rig4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"rig4:def:horizon\">99</a> and the prescribed asymptotic hypotheses has invariant ADM mass $M_0$, horizon area $\\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$, and equality in Theorem <a href=\"#four:thm:main\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"four:thm:main\">98</a>.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.3"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-rig4-thm-rigidity",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega,g,K)$ belong to Definition <a href=\"#rig4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"rig4:def:horizon\">99</a>, and put $m=\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}$. Then $$\\label{rig4:eq:intro-equality}\n m=\\frac12\\left(\\frac A\\omega\\right)^{2/3}$$ if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including $S$, into the regular maximal extension of $\\overline g_m$. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, the chosen end approaches its spatial infinity, and $S$ maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The pullback of the spacetime metric is $g$; for a consistent future unit normal $n$, the second fundamental form is precisely the original tensor $K$, with the convention $$\\label{rig4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form}\n K(U,V)=\\overline g_m(\\overline\\nabla_U n,V).$$ Both the embedding and the normal extend smoothly to $S$ in horizon-regular coordinates.*\n\n*Equivalently, every such Schwarzschild–Tangherlini hypersurface in $\\overline g_{M_0}$ satisfying Definition <a href=\"#rig4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"rig4:def:horizon\">99</a> and the prescribed asymptotic hypotheses has invariant ADM mass $M_0$, horizon area $\\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$, and equality in Theorem <a href=\"#four:thm:main\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"four:thm:main\">98</a>.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.3"
        }
      ],
      "exact_statement": "Let $(\\Omega,g,K)$ belong to Definition <a href=\"#rig4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"rig4:def:horizon\">99</a>, and put $m=\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}$. Then $$\\label{rig4:eq:intro-equality}\n m=\\frac12\\left(\\frac A\\omega\\right)^{2/3}$$ if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including $S$, into the regular maximal extension of $\\overline g_m$. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, the chosen end approaches its spatial infinity, and $S$ maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The pullback of the spacetime metric is $g$; for a consistent future unit normal $n$, the second fundamental form is precisely the original tensor $K$, with the convention $$\\label{rig4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form}\n K(U,V)=\\overline g_m(\\overline\\nabla_U n,V).$$ Both the embedding and the normal extend smoothly to $S$ in horizon-regular coordinates.*\n\n*Equivalently, every such Schwarzschild–Tangherlini hypersurface in $\\overline g_{M_0}$ satisfying Definition <a href=\"#rig4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"rig4:def:horizon\">99</a> and the prescribed asymptotic hypotheses has invariant ADM mass $M_0$, horizon area $\\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$, and equality in Theorem <a href=\"#four:thm:main\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"four:thm:main\">98</a>.",
      "explanation": "In the connected one-ended horizon class, equality is equivalent to smooth realization of the original data in the regular Tangherlini extension.",

        "anchor": "stmt-four-prop-existence",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the prepared geometry and $0<\\epsilon<1$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-four-thm-prepared-energy",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth, connected, and orientable, complete with a nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat. Let $K$ be a smooth compactly supported symmetric covariant tensor. Suppose, with a smooth positive function $r$ equal to the coordinate radius on the end, constants $c_0>0$ and $0<\\delta_1<1$, that $$\\mu-|J|_g\\ge c_0r^{-4-\\delta_1}\\quad\\hbox{on }M,\n \\qquad H+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_SK<0\\quad\\hbox{on every component of }S,$$ where the boundary normal points into $M$. Suppose on the end that $$g-\\delta=O_k(r^{-2})\\quad\\hbox{for every integer }k\\ge0,\n \\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{Scal}}_g=O(r^{-4-\\delta_1}),$$ and that the ADM energy $E_g$ is finite in the stated normalization. Let $A_*$ be the infimum of the total $g$-three-volume of the entire intrinsic boundaries of connected closed smooth outer domains containing the distant end, with interiors disjoint from $S$, including disconnected cuts and frontier coincident with $S$. Then $$\\label{four:ex:prepared-inequality}\n E_g\\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A_*}{\\omega_3}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.3"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-ads-thm-main",
        "exact_quote": "For every background, fixed TT seed, and solution branch satisfying <a href=\"#ads:eq:background\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ads:eq:background\">[ads:eq:background]</a>–<a href=\"#ads:eq:branch\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ads:eq:branch\">[ads:eq:branch]</a> and the mass assumptions above, there is $0<\\epsilon_0\\leq\\epsilon_*$ such that $$m_{\\mathrm{AH}}(\\epsilon)\\geq\n \\sqrt{\\frac{A_\\epsilon}{16\\pi}}\\left(1+\\frac{A_\\epsilon}{4\\pi}\\right)\n \\qquad(0\\leq\\epsilon<\\epsilon_0).$$ For all sufficiently small positive $\\epsilon$, equality holds if the seed is radial, and the inequality is strict otherwise.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ads-prop-quartic",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Exterior and enclosing area** ([source](#stmt-n3-intro-exterior-class)): An exterior is a connected orientable smooth three-manifold $\Omega$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary, complete as a metric space with its boundary included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat. An enclosing cut is a compact smooth embedded surface in $\overline\Omega$ separating the entire inner boundary from the sufficiently distant part of that end. Equivalently, it bounds the side containing the distant end; the other side is filled up to the inner obstacle. A cut may have several components and may coincide with the inner boundary. Its normal points toward the end. We put $$a_g(\partial\Omega)= \inf\{\|\Gamma\|_g:\Gamma\text{ is an enclosing cut}\}.$$ When using perimeter compactness, we take the closure of this class among filled inner sets and include the area of any frontier coinciding with the obstacle. Smooth outward approximation gives the same infimum. Enclosing cuts and minimizing sets are taken with bounded complementary pockets filled. Auxiliary perimeter arguments may use competitors containing the inner obstacle before filling: filling a bounded pocket deletes its frontier, cannot increase perimeter, and leaves the enclosing infimum unchanged.
- **Admissible boundary and designated-end enclosing area** ([source](#stmt-bridge-intro-global-admissible)): Fix an asymptotically flat end of $M$. An admissible boundary is a nonempty compact smooth embedded two-sided surface $S=\partial D^+$, possibly disconnected, where $D^+$ is a smooth open region containing the entire sufficiently distant part of the chosen end. The region $D^+$ need not be connected and may contain other ends. For the normal $\nu$ pointing into $D^+$, require $$H_S+\operatorname{tr}_S K\le0.$$ Define $$\label{bridge:intro:global-area} A_{\min}(S)=\inf\left\{ \operatorname{Area}_g(\partial D'^+): \begin{array}{l} D'^+\subset D^+,\quad D'^+\text{ contains the chosen end at infinity},\\ \partial D'^+\text{ is a compact smooth embedded boundary} \end{array}\right\}.$$ Competitors may be disconnected or coincide with $S$. They need not be trapped or minimal. No condition on the inward null expansion is imposed.
- **Partial-coincidence outermostness** ([source](#stmt-n3-rigidity-partial-outermostness)): Let the boundary of a one-ended exterior be $S=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{\ell}S_i$, with $1\leq\ell<\infty$ and each $S_i$ connected. The boundary is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense if no enclosing cut $\Gamma\ne S$ has all of the following properties: every connected component of $\Gamma$ is either an entire original component $S_i$ or is wholly contained in the open exterior; at least one component lies in the open exterior; and $\theta_+(\Gamma)\leq0$ everywhere for the normal toward the end.
- **Charged exterior** ([source](#stmt-ch-pre-charged-exterior)): A charged exterior consists of a connected orientable smooth three-manifold $N$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$, a Riemannian metric $g$ complete with $S$ included, a symmetric covariant tensor $K$, and vector fields $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$. There is exactly one end. In coordinates $x$ on that end, with $r_x=\|x\|$, for some $q>1/2$, $$\label{ch:pre:falloff} g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_2(r_x^{-q}),\quad K_{ij}=O_1(r_x^{-1-q}),\quad \mathcal E^i,\mathcal B^i=O_1(r_x^{-2}).$$ The notation $O_k(r^{-b})$ bounds coordinate derivatives of order $j\le k$ by $Cr^{-b-j}$. Define the total constraint densities by $$\label{ch:pre:constraints} 16\pi\mu=R_g+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)^2-\|K\|_g^2, \qquad 8\pi J_i=\nabla^j\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr).$$ The functions $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$ are integrable. The matter densities are $$\label{ch:pre:matter} \mu_m=\mu-\frac{\|\mathcal E\|_g^2+\|\mathcal B\|_g^2}{8\pi}, \qquad J_m=J-\frac{(\mathcal E\times\mathcal B)^\flat}{4\pi},$$ where the cross product uses the orientation and metric. They satisfy $$\label{ch:pre:charged-dec} \mu_m\ge \|J_m\|_g,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\mathcal E=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\mathcal B=0.$$ The boundary satisfies $\theta_+(S)\le0$. We define ADM energy and momentum by the following finite limits (Arnowitt, Deser, and Misner 1962) [[ArnowittDeserMisner1962](#ref-ArnowittDeserMisner1962)]: $$\begin{aligned} E&=\frac1{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=R}(\partial_jg_{ij}-\partial_ig_{jj})n_\delta^i\,dA_\delta, \label{ch:pre:adm-energy}\\ P_i&=\frac1{8\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=R}\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr)n_\delta^j\,dA_\delta, \label{ch:pre:adm-momentum}\\ Q_E&=\frac1{4\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=R}g(\mathcal E,\nu_R)\,dA_g, \qquad Q_B=\frac1{4\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=R}g(\mathcal B,\nu_R)\,dA_g. \label{ch:pre:charges} \end{aligned}$$ In the first two formulas the normal and area element are Euclidean; in the last two, $\nu_R$ is the outward $g$-unit normal. No extension of the physical data across $S$ is required.
- **Enclosing cuts in four spatial dimensions** ([source](#stmt-four-def-cuts)): Let $M$ have nonempty compact boundary $S$ and finitely many asymptotically flat ends, and fix an end $e$. An admissible outer domain $D_e$ is a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold with boundary, closed as a subset of $M$, such that its manifold interior lies in $\operatorname{int}M$, it contains the entire sufficiently distant part of $e$, and it contains no sufficiently distant part of any other end. Its entire intrinsic manifold boundary $\Gamma=\partial_{\mathrm{man}}D_e$ is required to be compact. The enclosing volume is $$A_e(S)=\inf_{D_e}\|\partial_{\mathrm{man}}D_e\|_g.$$ All frontier coincident with $S$ is counted. The cut may be disconnected. In the one-ended case $D_e=M$ is allowed and has intrinsic boundary $S$. We then also write $A_*$ for this infimum.
- **Connected outermost horizon class** ([source](#stmt-rig4-def-horizon)): Let $(\Omega^4,g,K)$ satisfy the initial-data hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#four:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:thm:main">98</a>, with exactly one end and connected boundary $S$. We additionally require: 1. $S$ is a future marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS): $\theta_+(S)=0$ for the normal into $\Omega$. 2. $S$ is outermost toward the end: no smooth compact embedded two-sided enclosing hypersurface in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, possibly disconnected and oriented toward the end, has $\theta_+\le0$ everywhere. 3. $S$ is outer area-minimizing: every cut in Definition <a href="#four:def:cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:def:cuts">97</a> has area at least $A:=\|S\|_g>0$. Consequently $A_e(S)=A$.
- **Initial data set** ([source](#intro:overview)): An initial data set consists of a Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ and a symmetric two-tensor $K$, representing the metric and second fundamental form of a spacelike hypersurface.
- **Future outward null expansion** ([source](#intro:overview)): For a hypersurface $S\subset M$ and a unit normal $\nu$ toward the chosen exterior, its future outward null expansion is $$\theta_+(S)=H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_S K,$$ where $H_S$ is positive on Euclidean spheres with outward normal.
- **Weakly future outer trapped surface** ([source](#intro:overview)): We call $S$ weakly future outer trapped when $\theta_+(S)\le0$.
- **Future MOTS** ([source](#intro:overview)): A future marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) satisfies $\theta_+=0$.

          "anchor": "stmt-four-thm-main",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth and connected, with $M$ orientable, $K$ an arbitrary smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $S=\\partial M$ nonempty, compact, and smooth. <a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **R1** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-rest-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-rest-reduction): Conformal strictification, annular replacement, vacuum bending and repair -> Strict rest-end approximations
- **R2** [claim](#stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain): Total trapped regions, right-continuity thresholds and stable collars -> Prepared geometric exterior
- **R3** [claim](#stmt-n3-existence-deformation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-existence-deformation): A priori bounds, elliptic regularity and compact degree -> Smooth coupled deformation and exhaustion limit
- **R4** [claim](#stmt-n3-limit-energy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-limit-energy): Flux control, minimal enclosure and Riemannian comparison -> Neutral exterior energy inequality
- **R5** [claim](#stmt-bridge-bridge-timelike) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bridge-bridge-timelike): Positive enclosing area and strict conformal path -> Timelikeness without an extra assumption
- **R6** [claim](#stmt-n3-static-classification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-static-schwarzschild-base): Original-data variation, causal stationary field, static double and hypersurface reconstruction -> Schwarzschild exterior realization
- **R7** [claim](#stmt-ch-rest-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ch-rest-strict-direction-2): Charge-preserving conformal and end replacement -> Strict charged rest data
- **R8** [claim](#stmt-ch-ell-neutral-input) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ch-ell-neutral-input): Verification of neutral input hypotheses and transfer of elliptic construction -> Charged deformation solutions
- **R9** [claim](#stmt-ch-cmp-charged-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ch-cmp-charged-comparison): Closed flux-form transport and electromagnetic square estimate -> Divergence-free charged comparison fields
- **R10** [claim](#stmt-ch-final-minimal-enclosure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ch-final-minimal-enclosure): Minimal enclosure, charged Riemannian inequality and ordered limits -> Charged upper-area inequality
- **R11** [claim](#stmt-four-prop-rest-end) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-prop-rest-end): Constraint moment corrections, vacuum bending and conformal repair -> Controlled rest-end approximations
- **R12** [claim](#stmt-four-prop-geometric-preparation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-prop-geometric-preparation): Threshold regions, support transport and trace allowance -> Prepared black and white exterior
- **R13** [claim](#stmt-four-prop-existence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-prop-existence): Axial regularity, scalar trial map and compact return-map degree -> Smooth coupled solutions and exhaustion
- **R14** [claim](#stmt-four-thm-prepared-energy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-thm-prepared-energy): Energy comparison, minimal enclosure and Bray-Lee comparison -> Prepared four-dimensional energy bound
- **R15** [claim](#stmt-rig4-rec-embedding) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rig4-rec-embedding): Original equality variation, static classification and regular horizon attachment -> Original Tangherlini hypersurface
- **R16** [claim](#stmt-ads-prop-expansions) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ads-prop-expansions): Weighted coefficient equations and exact mass Green formula -> Actual deficit expansion
- **R17** [claim](#stmt-ads-prop-quadratic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ads-prop-quadratic): CMC sphere jets, Hawking variation and TT square -> Nonnegative quadratic coefficient
- **R18** [claim](#stmt-ads-prop-quartic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ads-lem-dipole-obstruction-2): Corrected slice jets, null boundary transport and dipole obstruction -> Quartic positivity for nonradial kernel directions
- **R19** [claim](#stmt-ads-prop-radial) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ads-prop-radial): Uniqueness under rotations and conserved radial mass -> Exact radial equality

Set $$\\label{n3:domains:assigned-heights}\n b_-=c_b-C_b<0,\n \\qquad b_+=-c_w-C_w>0.$$ There is a smooth positive function $\\rho$, equal to a positive constant times $r^{-4}$ on the far end and satisfying symbol derivative bounds there, such that, for every $h\\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$\\label{n3:domains:offset-smallness}\n |(h+C)\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}K|+|\\nabla C|+\\rho\n      \\leq\\tfrac12\\mathfrak m\n \\quad\\hbox{everywhere on }\\Omega.$$ The thresholds, collars, offset, and $\\rho$ are fixed before the deformation parameters are chosen.           "anchor": "stmt-ch-ell-neutral-input",
          "exact_quote": "For the prepared class in Definition <a href=\"#ch:ell:prepared-neutral\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ch:ell:prepared-neutral\">84</a>, with the profiles, parameters, penalty choices, and physical endpoint in Equations <a href=\"#ch:ell:profiles\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ch:ell:profiles\">[ch:ell:profiles]</a>–<a href=\"#ch:ell:system\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ch:ell:system\">[ch:ell:system]</a>, the following statements hold.*\n\n1.  *<span class=\"upright\">Existence with the floor bound.</span> With $\\delta_0,C_n$ chosen as in Proposition <a href=\"#n3:deformation:floor\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:deformation:floor\">28</a>, for every sufficiently small fixed $\\epsilon>0$, Theorem <a href=\"#n3:existence:deformation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:existence:deformation\">38</a> supplies $n_0$, enlarged to include $n\\ge4$ and $n>2/\\epsilon$, and a sufficient radius $R_{\\min}(n,\\epsilon)\\to\\infty$ as $n\\to\\infty$, such that Equation <a href=\"#ch:ell:system\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ch:ell:system\">[ch:ell:system]</a> has a smooth solution on every $X_R$ with $n\\ge n_0$ and $R\\ge R_{\\min}(n,\\epsilon)$. It satisfies $t>-\\epsilon$ on $\\overline{X_R}$. The radius includes the geometric supports, all a priori and floor thresholds, and the outer-boundary floor restriction in the proof of that theorem. No polynomial bound for this radius is asserted.*\n\n\n2.  *<span class=\"upright\">Physical-endpoint height and slope bounds.</span> For smooth finite-truncation solutions with $t\\ge-\\epsilon$, for these sufficiently large $n,R$, Lemma <a href=\"#n3:apriori:collars\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:apriori:collars\">30</a> at the physical endpoint gives fixed $c,C_*>0$ such that $$\\label{ch:ell:slopes}\n     \\frac c{\\tau_0}\\le\\partial_\\nu f\\le\\frac{C_*}{\\tau_0}\n           \\quad(B_b),\\qquad\n     \\frac c{\\tau_0}\\le-\\partial_\\nu f\\le\\frac{C_*}{\\tau_0}\n           \\quad(B_w).$$ These constants are independent of $n,R$ after fixing the prepared data and $\\epsilon$. Also $b_-\\le h\\le b_+$ on every fixed compact region needed for the scalar-curvature argument, in particular on the supports of $K,C$. A condition on an absent face color is vacuous. No global height bound is being added to this statement.*\n\n\n\n3.  *<span class=\"upright\">Exhaustion and end normalization.</span> At fixed $\\epsilon,n$, the solutions have local smooth estimates of every fixed order, uniformly as $R\\to\\infty$, including up to the fixed inner boundary. Every sequence of allowed radii tending to infinity has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of $\\overline X$ to a solution of Equation <a href=\"#ch:ell:system\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ch:ell:system\">[ch:ell:system]</a> with the outer boundary condition omitted and $t\\ge-\\epsilon$. The preceding compact height and face estimates pass to this limit. For sufficiently large $n\\ge\\max\\{4,\\lceil2/\\epsilon\\rceil\\}$, choose an exhausting sequence and the limiting solution supplied by Lemma <a href=\"#n3:limit:end\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:limit:end\">39</a>. For some $c_n>0$ and constants $C_j(n)$, this solution also satisfies $$\\label{ch:ell:end-estimates}\n     |\\nabla^jf|\\le C_j(n)e^{-c_nr_y}\\quad\\text{for each fixed }j,\n     \\qquad t,Z=O_2(r_y^{-1}).$$ Writing $\\bar g=g+l^2df^2$, both $t-Z$ and $\\bar g-g$, together with their coordinate derivatives of every fixed order, decay exponentially. Moreover $$\\label{ch:ell:end-flux}\n     V=4\\nabla_gt+O(r_y^{-3}),\\qquad\n     \\lim_{s\\to\\infty}\\int_{r_y=s}g(V,\\nu_s)\\,dA_g\n     \\quad\\text{exists and is finite},$$ where $\\nu_s$ points toward infinity.",

        }

          "anchor": "stmt-four-prop-geometric-preparation",
          "exact_quote": "For the prepared data satisfying <a href=\"#four:geo:prepared-gap\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"four:geo:prepared-gap\">[four:geo:prepared-gap]</a>, there are a closed connected exterior $\\Omega\\subset M$ with one end and nonempty compact smooth boundary $B$, two negative numbers $c_b,c_w$, and a decomposition of $B$ into black and white components with the following properties. With the normal $\\nu$ into $\\Omega$ and $P_B=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_B K$, $$\\label{four:geo:two-boundary-expansions}\n H+P_B=c_b\\quad\\text{on black components},\\qquad\n H-P_B=c_w\\quad\\text{on white components}.$$ The components come from closed total-region families $\\mathcal D_c$ and $\\mathcal W_c$ at right-continuity thresholds $c_b$ and $c_w$, respectively. The white family is formed with the black region fixed, and is allowed to be empty.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-four-thm-prepared-energy",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth, connected, and orientable, complete with a nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat. Let $K$ be a smooth compactly supported symmetric covariant tensor. Suppose, with a smooth positive function $r$ equal to the coordinate radius on the end, constants $c_0>0$ and $0<\\delta_1<1$, that $$\\mu-|J|_g\\ge c_0r^{-4-\\delta_1}\\quad\\hbox{on }M,\n \\qquad H+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_SK<0\\quad\\hbox{on every component of }S,$$ where the boundary normal points into $M$. Suppose on the end that $$g-\\delta=O_k(r^{-2})\\quad\\hbox{for every integer }k\\ge0,\n \\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{Scal}}_g=O(r^{-4-\\delta_1}),$$ and that the ADM energy $E_g$ is finite in the stated normalization. Let $A_*$ be the infimum of the total $g$-three-volume of the entire intrinsic boundaries of connected closed smooth outer domains containing the distant end, with interiors disjoint from $S$, including disconnected cuts and frontier coincident with $S$. Then $$\\label{four:ex:prepared-inequality}\n E_g\\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A_*}{\\omega_3}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",

        }

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-ads-prop-expansions",
          "exact_quote": "For every prescribed seed and branch in the theorem, set $p=2$ and take $u_j,F_j,B_j$ from Lemma <a href=\"#ads:lem:rotation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ads:lem:rotation\">182</a>. If the seed has the form <a href=\"#ads:ana:kernel-seed\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ads:ana:kernel-seed\">[ads:ana:kernel-seed]</a>, we may instead take $p=4$ with the finite coefficient construction. In both cases, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\left\\|\\psi-\\sum_{j=1}^p\\epsilon^ju_j\\right\\|_\\beta\n     &=O(\\epsilon^{p+1}),\\notag\\\\\n \\left\\|L\\psi-\\sum_{j=1}^p\\epsilon^jF_j\\right\\|_{2\\beta}\n     &=O(\\epsilon^{p+1}),\\notag\\\\\n \\left\\|\\partial_s\\psi|_S-\\sum_{j=1}^p\\epsilon^jB_j\\right\\|_{C^0(S)}\n     &=O(\\epsilon^{p+1}).\n \\label{ads:ana:three-remainders}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The area and all four mass components have actual expansions to the same order. Their mass coefficients are $$a_{\\mu j}[q]=\\mathcal G_\\mu(u_j,F_j,B_j),\\qquad\n p_\\mu(\\epsilon)=p_\\mu(0)+\\sum_{j=1}^p\\epsilon^j a_{\\mu j}[q]\n                      +O(\\epsilon^{p+1}).\n \\label{ads:ana:mass-coefficients}$$*\n\n\n*In particular, the actual deficit satisfies $$\\mathfrak D_q(\\epsilon)=c_2[q]\\epsilon^2+O(\\epsilon^3)\n \\label{ads:ana:deficit-second}$$ for every seed under consideration. The coefficient $c_2$ is a continuous quadratic form on $\\mathscr T_{\\tau,\\alpha}$ in the $\\|\\cdot\\|_\\beta$ topology, invariant under rotations. For seeds of the form <a href=\"#ads:ana:kernel-seed\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ads:ana:kernel-seed\">[ads:ana:kernel-seed]</a> there is additionally the actual expansion $$\\mathfrak D_q(\\epsilon)\n     =c_2[q]\\epsilon^2+c_3[q]\\epsilon^3+c_4[q]\\epsilon^4+O(\\epsilon^5).\n \\label{ads:ana:deficit-fourth}$$ The subsequent geometric arguments determine the signs and the vanishing of these coefficients.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.3"
        }
      ],
      "id": "R16",
      "inputs": [
        "Fixed TT seed and prescribed branch"
      ],
      "method": "Weighted coefficient equations and exact mass Green formula",
      "output": "Actual deficit expansion",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-ads-prop-expansions"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-ads-prop-quadratic",
      "depends_on": [
        "R16"
      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-ads-prop-quadratic",
          "exact_quote": "On the real linear space of all smooth TT seeds with the prescribed decay, the first deficit coefficient is zero and the second coefficient $c_2[q]$ is a continuous, rotation-invariant, nonnegative quadratic form. For a finite-angular-type seed it is given by $$\\begin{gathered}\n c_2[q]=\\frac1{16\\pi}\\int_M N\\left(\n |q-Q(v)|^2+|U|^2+2FJ_s^0F\\right)\\,\\,\\mathrm dV_0,\\\\\n J_s^0=-\\Delta_{r^2\\sigma}-\\frac2{r^2}+\\frac{6m_0}{r^3}.\n \\end{gathered}\n \\label{ads:eq:quadratic-positive-form}$$ The last term is integrated on the spheres before radial integration. For every actual branch in Theorem <a href=\"#ads:thm:main\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ads:thm:main\">176</a>, $$\\mathfrak D_q(\\epsilon)=c_2[q]\\epsilon^2+o(\\epsilon^2).\n \\label{ads:eq:actual-quadratic-deficit}$$ In particular, $c_2[q]>0$ implies a strictly positive deficit for all sufficiently small positive $\\epsilon$.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.3"
        }

          "exact_quote": "Suppose that $c_2[q]=0$. Write the representation furnished by Corollary <a href=\"#ads:cor:kernel\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ads:cor:kernel\">191</a> as $$q=Q(v):=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}_{g_0}v-Bv,\\qquad Lv=0,\n \\qquad v=v_0(s)+v_1(s,x),$$ where $v_1$ has only degree-one spherical modes and $v$ decays at infinity. Then $$c_0[q]=c_1[q]=c_2[q]=c_3[q]=0,\n \\qquad c_4[q]\\geq 0.$$ If $v_1\\not\\equiv0$, then $c_4[q]>0$. In particular, in that case the actual deficit $\\mathfrak D_q(\\epsilon)$ is strictly positive for all sufficiently small positive $\\epsilon$.",

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **I-CUT**: Use the full enclosing infimum for the theorem-specific cut class; count boundary-coincident pieces.
- **I-N3**: Apply the neutral exterior mass-area inequality with its specified boundary normal and future trapping condition, together with all exterior, DEC, decay, integrability and ADM-limit hypotheses.
- **I-CH**: Retain electromagnetic momentum in the physical matter condition and retain the charged upper-area formulation outside the stated lower-bound branch.
- **I-RIG**: Test rigidity on the original data under the additional horizon hypotheses; numerical deformations do not carry the equality conclusion.
- **I-ADS**: Keep the background, TT seed and solution branch fixed; the local parameter interval need not be uniform.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **A-CUT**: Replace the enclosing infimum by a sampled surface area. -> A sampled competitor can exceed the infimum, giving a stronger unsupported mass bound.
- **A-END**: Reuse an area value with different excluded ends. -> The optimized competitor class changes.
- **A-CH-BRANCH**: Use the charged mass lower-bound expression for every positive area radius. -> The lower-bound branch restriction is lost.
- **A-CH-DEC**: Ignore electromagnetic momentum when checking matter DEC. -> The charged theorem hypotheses are not checked.
- **A-RIG**: Infer a Schwarzschild realization from approximate mass-area equality. -> Approximate scalar agreement does not certify exact equality or horizon hypotheses.
- **A-RIG4**: Apply the four-dimensional equality classification to disconnected horizon data. -> The equality scope is expanded beyond the stated horizon class.
- **A-ADS**: Use a common perturbation cutoff across changing seeds or branches. -> A local theorem becomes an unsupported uniform theorem.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. Not applicable to a finite executable certificate of the paper results. Definition 1 takes an infimum over smooth enclosing cuts; Theorem 38 constructs smooth PDE solutions on truncations and obtains subsequences as the radius tends to infinity; Theorem 176 supplies a sufficiently small interval for each fixed background, TT seed and solution branch. These source-bound continuum hypotheses and limiting constructions do not supply a finite input encoding, effective truncation-error certificate, or finite decision procedure for the enclosing infimum and exact geometric rigidity. Arithmetic evaluation of the displayed bounds alone cannot certify those hypotheses.

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **L01** (hypothesis): The neutral exterior inequality requires the specified complete one-ended exterior, constraint and decay assumptions, integrable densities, finite ADM limits and weak future trapping with the normal toward the end. Blocked use: ['Applying the inequality to arbitrary sampled metrics without checking the continuum hypotheses.']
- **L02** (edge_case): Enclosing area counts the entire obstacle and permits disconnected cuts and coincidence with the obstacle; boundary area alone need not equal the enclosing infimum. Blocked use: ['Replacing the enclosing infimum with one selected surface area without outer area-minimization.', 'Dropping obstacle-coincident frontier area.']
- **L03** (hypothesis): Neutral equality rigidity requires exact equality, future MOTS components, partial-coincidence outermostness and outer area-minimization; the weaker wholly-interior exclusion is not asserted. Blocked use: ['Inferring rigidity from numerical near-equality.', 'Using only wholly-interior outermostness to invoke the finite-component equality theorem.']
- **L04** (hypothesis): The electric-magnetic charged exterior result requires a single end, divergence-free fields and the physical matter dominant energy condition. Blocked use: ['Using only the total neutral dominant energy condition for charged inputs.', 'Extending the electric-magnetic theorem to unrestricted multiple-ended data.']
- **L05** (counterexample_scope): The charged upper-area conclusion cannot generally be replaced by the familiar mass lower bound on the small-radius branch. Blocked use: ['Asserting the lower-bound formulation for every positive area radius.']
- **L06** (hypothesis): The finite-end electric extension excludes magnetic fields and requires zero ADM momentum only at the designated end, together with the specified area-charge branch. Blocked use: ['Transferring the extension to nonzero designated-end momentum.', 'Transferring the extension to magnetic data.', 'Imposing an unnecessary zero-momentum condition at every other end.']
- **L07** (edge_case): The designated-end enclosing volume counts every intrinsic boundary component, including frontier coincident with the original boundary, and treats other ends as obstacles. Blocked use: ['Computing the designated-end quantity using a cut that retains the distant tail of another end.', 'Discarding components of the intrinsic boundary.']
- **L08** (hypothesis): The higher-dimensional neutral inequality here is limited to the stated spatial dimension and falloff regime; no arbitrary-dimensional extension is supplied. Blocked use: ['Using the same coefficient or exponent in arbitrary spatial dimensions.', 'Using weaker falloff without another theorem.']
- **L09** (hypothesis): Tangherlini equality rigidity is restricted to the connected outermost horizon class with one end, a future MOTS boundary and outer area-minimization. Blocked use: ['Applying equality rigidity to disconnected or multi-ended exteriors.', 'Dropping outermostness or outer area-minimization.']
- **L10** (formal_scope): The Tangherlini rigidity conclusion concerns only the exterior and does not classify data behind the horizon. Blocked use: ['Claiming a global classification of the interior behind the horizon.']
- **L11** (approximation): The end exhaustion, deformation parameter and strictification limits have a prescribed order; fixed-parameter regularity constants do not justify arbitrary joint limits. Blocked use: ['Interchanging limits without uniform estimates.', 'Assuming every fixed-parameter regularity constant has polynomial growth.']
- **L12** (nonconstructive): Continuum existence via compactness and topological degree is not a finite certified solver or a finite certificate for the enclosing-area infimum. Blocked use: ['Treating sampled PDE convergence or a finite area search as a proof of the full continuum theorem.', 'Claiming a finite computational complexity bound for the continuum construction.']
- **L13** (hypothesis): The anti-de Sitter result is local for each fixed transverse-traceless seed and prescribed decaying solution branch; no common neighborhood over arbitrary varying seeds is supplied. Blocked use: ['Promoting the theorem to a global anti-de Sitter inequality.', 'Using a universal perturbation cutoff for arbitrary varying seeds or branches.']
- **L14** (hypothesis): The geometric minimum-enclosing-area AdS corollary adds a boundary sign condition, outermostness and outer area-minimization; these are not requirements of the coefficient theorem itself. Blocked use: ['Claiming minimum-enclosing-area equality from the coefficient theorem alone.', 'Imposing the corollary boundary sign condition on the broader coefficient theorem.']
- **L15** (approximation): Weighted uniform Taylor estimates do not furnish spatial derivative control needed for mass flux; the radius limit is taken before expansion. Blocked use: ['Differentiating weighted uniform remainders without stronger regularity.', 'Interchanging the radius limit with perturbation or angular approximation limits without estimates.']
- **L16** (formal_scope): The changed AdS slice is a finite jet calculation; its transformed trace is eliminated only to the stated remainder order, without a higher-order maximality claim or an actual Einstein extension behind the boundary. Blocked use: ['Claiming maximality through the full jet order.', 'Interpreting formal time jets as an actual spacetime extension behind the boundary.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove sharp spacetime Penrose inequalities for invariant ADM mass and minimum enclosing area in three and four spatial dimensions. Under their respective designated-end conventions, the neutral numerical results allow arbitrary second fundamental form, nonzero momentum, disconnected weakly future trapped boundary, and finitely many ends. Under the stated horizon hypotheses, equality for the neutral inequalities reconstructs the original exterior data as spacelike slices of Schwarzschild spacetime in three dimensions and Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime in four; the four-dimensional equality theorem concerns a connected, one-ended exterior. We also prove a three-dimensional electric–magnetic charged upper-area inequality for one-ended data with nonzero momentum, with separate purely electric rest-frame corollaries allowing finitely many ends. Finally, for each fixed transverse-traceless seed and prescribed decaying solution branch, we prove a local Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter inequality.

<a id="intro:overview"></a>
##### Introduction

The Penrose inequality compares the mass seen at infinity with the size of a region hidden behind a trapped boundary. An initial data set consists of a Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ and a symmetric two-tensor $K$, representing the metric and second fundamental form of a spacelike hypersurface. For a hypersurface $S\subset M$ and a unit normal $\nu$ toward the chosen exterior, its future outward null expansion is $$\theta_+(S)=H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_S K,$$ where $H_S$ is positive on Euclidean spheres with outward normal. We call $S$ weakly future outer trapped when $\theta_+(S)\le0$. A future marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) satisfies $\theta_+=0$. The dominant energy condition requires the energy density of the constraint equations to be at least the norm of their momentum density. Precise normalizations and asymptotic assumptions are given separately for each spatial dimension below. The asymptotically flat results resolve the minimum-enclosing-area form of the spacetime Penrose conjecture in three and four spatial dimensions under those hypotheses.

The geometric quantity throughout the asymptotically flat results is an enclosing infimum. An enclosing cut separates the entire designated inner boundary from the chosen distant end. Its full area is counted, including portions coincident with the original boundary. Cuts may be disconnected and need not themselves be trapped. This distinction matters: a trapped surface need not minimize area among enclosing surfaces. When several ends are present, the definition also specifies which of them lie on the excluded side. We give the exact admissible classes in each theorem, rather than identifying infima with different end constraints. In this overview, $A_{\min}$ denotes the enclosing infimum appropriate to the result being described; each part defines its precise cut class.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
###### The results and their relation

For an asymptotically flat end, let $(E,P)$ denote its ADM energy and momentum. Once $E>|P|$, its invariant mass is $m=\sqrt{E^2-|P|^2}$. In three spatial dimensions, the basic numerical bound is $$m\ge\sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}}{16\pi}}.$$ Here $A_{\min}$ denotes the relevant minimum enclosing area. The one-ended theorem is proved first under a timelike assumption on $(E,P)$. A positive conformal deformation then rules out a non-timelike ADM vector, and cutting off the unwanted distant ends gives the complete-data formulation. The latter permits a disconnected chosen exterior region as well as a disconnected trapped boundary. The precise statements are Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">2</a>, Corollary <a href="#bridge:bridge:timelike" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bridge:bridge:timelike">46</a>, and Theorem <a href="#bridge:intro:global-penrose" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bridge:intro:global-penrose">44</a>.

Equality concerns the original data and requires additional geometric hypotheses. In Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:rigidity">48</a>, the chosen exterior is connected and one-ended, and its finite marginally trapped boundary is outer area-minimizing. Its outermostness condition excludes an enclosing weakly trapped cut that replaces any nonempty subset of the boundary components, even if other components remain coincident. Equality then forces a single spherical boundary component and a Schwarzschild spacetime realization of the entire exterior. The proof does not prescribe the data on the other side of that boundary.

For electric and magnetic fields, write $Q_E,Q_B$ for their total charges, $Q=(Q_E^2+Q_B^2)^{1/2}$, and $r=(A_{\min}/4\pi)^{1/2}$. Theorem <a href="#ch:intro:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ch:intro:main">71</a> proves $$m\ge Q,\qquad r\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$$ on a one-ended exterior. Its matter condition includes the electromagnetic momentum density. It allows arbitrary $K$ and nonzero ADM momentum. The familiar lower bound $m\ge(r+Q^2/r)/2$ follows on the branch $r\ge Q$; it is not an equivalent formulation for every positive $r$. Purely electric rest-frame consequences, including a designated-end theorem with finitely many ends, follow with their own explicit cut convention. No charged equality classification is asserted.

In four spatial dimensions, an enclosing hypersurface has three-dimensional volume $A_e$. With $\omega_3=2\pi^2$, the theorem is $$m_e\ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_e}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}.$$ Theorem <a href="#four:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:thm:main">98</a> allows arbitrary second fundamental form, finitely many asymptotically flat ends, and disconnected weakly future outer trapped boundary. Its hypotheses impose neither symmetry nor maximality. Theorem <a href="#rig4:thm:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rig4:thm:rigidity">100</a> completes this bound in the connected, one-ended horizon class: if the boundary is a future MOTS, outermost and outer area-minimizing, equality holds exactly for original exterior data realized by a smooth spacelike hypersurface in the regular Schwarzschild–Tangherlini extension. The embedding recovers both $g$ and $K$, reaches spatial infinity, and attaches smoothly to a future-horizon section or the bifurcation sphere. Boosted ends and non-time-symmetric slices are included. These additional horizon assumptions belong only to the equality theorem; no disconnected equality or behind-horizon classification is asserted in four dimensions.

The last part treats a different asymptotic geometry. For cosmological constant $-3$, fix a positive-mass Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter background, a transverse-traceless tensor, and a decaying positive conformal solution branch generated by that tensor. Here “transverse-traceless” means divergence free and trace free in the background metric. Theorem <a href="#ads:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ads:thm:main">176</a> gives, on a sufficiently small interval depending on these fixed choices, $$m_{\mathrm{AH}}\ge\sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}
                       \left(1+\frac{A}{4\pi}\right).$$ The quantity $m_{\mathrm{AH}}$ is the positive Lorentz norm of the hyperbolic mass covector, and $A$ is the area of the prescribed marginally trapped boundary. The theorem establishes equality precisely for radial seeds at sufficiently small positive parameters. Identifying $A$ with an enclosing infimum is a separate corollary with additional geometric hypotheses. The interval is not uniform over seeds or branches.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
###### How the proofs fit together

The asymptotically flat numerical proofs have a common structure. First, the distant end is replaced and repaired so that its energy approaches the original invariant mass in a rest frame. The replacement preserves the dominant energy condition and controls every enclosing cut. Next, trapped-region boundaries and disjoint collars prepare a fixed exterior for a coupled elliptic deformation. The unknown graph function and conformal factor produce a Riemannian comparison metric with nonnegative scalar curvature, a controlled energy change, and an enclosing area no smaller than the required original infimum. The Riemannian Penrose inequality completes the comparison.

The three-dimensional elliptic construction is proved in full once. The charged argument uses this same system: it verifies its hypotheses, transports closed flux forms through the geometric changes, and proves a square estimate incorporating the electromagnetic momentum. In four dimensions the scalar identity and regularity estimates change, so we give the corresponding construction separately. Its final metric has zero second fundamental form. A minimizing enclosure therefore brings that actual metric directly within the Riemannian theorem’s hypotheses.

The equality proofs start from the unmodified exterior. Variations of the constraints and of the enclosing-area infimum give a normalized causal stationary field. A twist estimate makes its positive-norm region static, without assuming regularity of an interior zero set. A complete conformal double then forces Euclidean geometry. In three dimensions, the zero-mass argument uses the spin structure supplied by orientability, and the boundary identities give each component the total original area, forcing one component. In four dimensions, we prove the required compactification and reduce zero-mass rigidity to the smooth positive-mass theorem with arbitrary other ends. The final step in both cases reconstructs the original $g,K$ and the smooth horizon attachment; it does not transfer equality through the numerical deformations. Figure <a href="#intro:proof-routes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:proof-routes">1</a> shows these two uses of the inequality.

Two ingredients keep the original-data argument independent of a chosen minimizing surface. Full obstacle perimeter includes every boundary-coincident piece. Compactness of all minimizing enclosures then gives the one-sided metric derivative as the minimum of their area derivatives. A positive measure on this minimizing space yields the variational identity; normal tests and the precise outermostness condition concentrate its area term on the original horizon. The causal-field estimates also separate a reusable finite-jet asymptotic argument from the charge normalization, so the converse can establish its asymptotic spacelike plane without assuming it.

The anti-de Sitter proof uses the Taylor coefficients of the given branch. Actual weighted remainder bounds connect those coefficients to the mass and area. The quadratic coefficient is a nonnegative quadratic form with a kernel of dimension four. A fourth-order argument treats its nonradial directions, while radial directions satisfy an exact mass conservation identity. This part is independent of the asymptotically flat elliptic construction.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### Relation to earlier work

Penrose proposed the mass–horizon comparison in the context of gravitational collapse and cosmic censorship (Penrose 1973) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Penrose1973](#ref-Penrose1973)].
