For example, simplicity of the kernel also follows by writing a kernel element as $v=\varphi w$ and applying the strong maximum principle to the resulting equation for $w$, whose zeroth-order term vanishes. Consider the augmented map $$\mathcal G(v,a)
   =\left(\Phi(v)-a,\ \int_\Sigma v\,\,\mathrm dA\right).$$ Its derivative at $(0,0)$ is <a id="n3:domains:augmented-linearization"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:augmented-linearization}
 (v,a)\longmapsto
 \left(Lv-a,\ \int_\Sigma v\,\,\mathrm dA\right).$$ This map is an isomorphism. Indeed, to solve $Lv-a=f$ with $\int v=b$, the Fredholm compatibility condition uniquely fixes $$a=-\frac{\int_\Sigma\varphi^*f\,\,\mathrm dA}
          {\int_\Sigma\varphi^*\,\,\mathrm dA}.$$ The equation for $v$ then has a solution; adding a multiple of $\varphi$ imposes its prescribed integral uniquely. Elliptic estimates and this one-dimensional normalization give a bounded inverse between the indicated Hölder spaces.

The implicit-function theorem consequently supplies smooth $v(s),a(s)$ with $\mathcal G(v(s),a(s))=(0,s)$. Differentiating at zero and pairing with $\varphi^*$ gives $a'(0)=0$ and $$v'(0)=\frac{\varphi}{\int_\Sigma\varphi\,\,\mathrm dA}>0.$$ After shortening the interval, all these graphs form an outward foliation and have constant expansion $c+a(s)$. If $a(s)\leq0$ at any positive $s$ in this interval, replace only this frontier component by $\Sigma(v(s))$. The collar is disjoint from all other components and designated barriers, so the new smooth bounding domain strictly contains the maximal region and its every free boundary component has expansion at most $c$. This contradicts maximality. Therefore $a(s)>0$ for every such $s>0$.

In either case positive graph velocity and compactness give the asserted bounds on $|\nabla s|$. Smooth elliptic bootstrapping of the graph equation gives smooth leaves in the zero-eigenvalue case. ◻

</details>

Apply this lemma separately with $Q=K$ to black faces and $Q=-K$ to white faces. There are finitely many faces, so choose disjoint collars in $\Omega$ and shorten them to have a common positive parameter range when convenient. Write $\nu_s=\nabla s/|\nabla s|$ for their outward leaf normal; it agrees with $\nu$ at $B$.

<a id="pm-h-22"></a>
###### From weak exterior supports to a smooth enclosure

The sublevel limits used below need not have smooth frontiers. We now show how an expansion bound on their exterior supports produces a smooth enclosure. The argument applies to arbitrary closed sets, without positive reach or a curvature bound on the supporting surfaces.

<a id="stmt-n3-domains-support-definition"></a>
<div id="n3:domains:support-definition" class="definition">

**Definition 16**. Let $D$ be closed in a smooth three-manifold and let $x\in\partial D$. A smooth exterior support is a smooth function $\phi$ near $x$ with $\phi(x)=0$, $\,\mathrm d\phi(x)\ne0$, and $D\subset\{\phi\leq0\}$ locally near $x$. Its normal is $n=\nabla\phi/|\nabla\phi|$. Define <a id="n3:domains:test-expansion"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:test-expansion}
 \mathcal E_Q[\phi](x)
   =\frac{(g^{ij}-n^in^j)\nabla_i\nabla_j\phi}{|\nabla\phi|}
       +\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}Q-Q(n,n).$$ We say $D$ has exterior-support expansion at most $c$ if every such support at every point of its frontier has $\mathcal E_Q[\phi]\leq c$.

</div>

For a smooth domain this is exactly the usual upper bound on its outward expansion: at contact an exterior supporting graph has mean curvature at most that of the enclosed smooth graph. The definition is unchanged by increasing smooth reparametrizations of $\phi$, because the additional Hessian term is a multiple of $\,\mathrm d\phi\otimes\,\mathrm d\phi$ and has zero tangential trace.

<a id="stmt-n3-domains-parallel-support"></a>
<div id="n3:domains:parallel-support" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:domains:parallel-estimate"></a>
**Lemma 17** (Parallel neighborhoods and additive error). *Suppose the frontier of a closed set $D$ lies in a fixed compact interior region of smooth $(N,g,Q)$ and has exterior-support expansion at most $c$. Put $D_z=\{y:\operatorname{dist}(y,D)\leq z\}$. For sufficiently small $z>0$, all exterior supports of $D_z$ have expansion at most $$\label{n3:domains:parallel-estimate}
 c+Cz.$$ The allowable radius and $C$ depend only on the compact ambient geometry and $Q$, and not on the support, its second fundamental form, or the regularity of $D$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-domains-parallel-support"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-domains-parallel-support</summary>

<a id="n3:domains:radial-normal"></a>
*Proof.* Take a support $\phi$ to $D_z$ at $x'$. There is a nearest point $x\in D$ and a length-$z$ minimizing unit-speed geodesic $\gamma:[0,z]\to N$ from $x$ to $x'$. For the radii under consideration the entire segment lies in a fixed smooth compact neighborhood and is shorter than its injectivity radius. The ball $\overline B_z(x)$ is contained in $D_z$ and touches its exterior support at $x'$. Its tangent plane there therefore agrees with that of the support and $$\label{n3:domains:radial-normal}
 \frac{\nabla\phi(x')}{|\nabla\phi(x')|}=\dot\gamma(z).$$ Let $P_t:T_xN\to T_{\gamma(t)}N$ denote parallel transport and put $P=P_z$.

<a id="n3:domains:jacobi-endpoints"></a>
<a id="n3:domains:jacobi-estimates"></a>
For every $X\in T_xN$ solve the Jacobi boundary problem $$\label{n3:domains:jacobi-endpoints}
 J_X''+\operatorname{Rm}(J_X,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma=0,
 \qquad J_X(0)=X,\qquad J_X(z)=PX.$$ Here primes denote covariant differentiation along $\gamma$. The short interval and absence of conjugate points make this problem uniquely solvable. Its estimates can be seen without division by an uncontrolled quantity. In a parallel frame write $j_X(t)=P_t^{-1}J_X(t)$ and $\mathcal R(t)$ for the curvature coefficient. The integral equation is $$j_X(t)=X+tA_X-
       \int_0^t(t-s)\mathcal R(s)j_X(s)\,\,\mathrm ds,
 \qquad
 A_X=\frac1z\int_0^z(z-s)\mathcal R(s)j_X(s)\,\,\mathrm ds.$$ It implies, by absorption for small $z$, $$\label{n3:domains:jacobi-estimates}
 \sup_{0\leq t\leq z}|j_X(t)|\leq2|X|,
 \qquad |A_X|\leq Cz|X|.$$ Also $\langle J_X,\dot\gamma\rangle$ is affine in $t$ and has equal endpoint values. Thus $\langle A_X,\dot\gamma(0)\rangle=0$.

We may therefore prescribe the first jet of a smooth unit vector field $V$ near $x$ by $$V(x)=\dot\gamma(0),\qquad \nabla_XV(x)=A_X.$$ To realize it with uniform second-jet bounds, choose a smooth local orthonormal frame obtained by radial parallel transport from $x$. In that frame take the affine coefficient vector with the prescribed value and first derivatives, and normalize its length. The orthogonality just proved means normalization preserves its prescribed first derivatives. The frame has uniformly bounded derivatives on a fixed small coordinate ball, and Equation <a href="#n3:domains:jacobi-estimates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:jacobi-estimates">[n3:domains:jacobi-estimates]</a> therefore gives uniformly bounded second derivatives of $V$. This construction uses the radial direction and the ambient geometry, with no derivatives of the support $\phi$.

Define the local endpoint map $$F_z(y)=\exp_y\bigl(zV(y)\bigr).$$ Its differential at $x$ is the terminal value of the Jacobi field with initial values $X,\nabla_XV(x)$. By Equation <a href="#n3:domains:jacobi-endpoints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:jacobi-endpoints">[n3:domains:jacobi-endpoints]</a>, it has the exact property <a id="n3:domains:exact-endpoint-isometry"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:exact-endpoint-isometry}
 F_z(x)=x',\qquad (\,\mathrm dF_z)_x=P,
 \qquad |(\nabla\,\mathrm dF_z)_x|\leq Cz.$$ The last bound follows by differentiating the smooth map $(y,v,z)\mapsto\exp_y(zv)$ twice in $y$, including the first and second derivatives of $V$. At $z=0$ the map is the identity and its covariant second derivative vanishes. Its $z$-derivative is uniformly bounded for the bounded jets just constructed, giving the displayed $Cz$ bound. The exact middle identity, rather than a near-isometry estimate, is essential.

The map $F_z$ takes $D$ locally into $D_z$, since its defining geodesic from any $y\in D$ has length $z$. Consequently $\psi=\phi\circ F_z$ is an exterior support to $D$ at $x$. Its derivative is $P^*\,\mathrm d\phi$, so its gradient length is exactly $|\nabla\phi(x')|$ and, by Equation <a href="#n3:domains:radial-normal" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:radial-normal">[n3:domains:radial-normal]</a>, its normal is $\dot\gamma(0)$. The covariant chain rule gives $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\psi(X,Y)
   =\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi(PX,PY)
        +\,\mathrm d\phi\bigl((\nabla\,\mathrm dF_z)(X,Y)\bigr)
 \quad\hbox{at }x.$$ Trace over an orthonormal basis of $\dot\gamma(0)^\perp$ and divide by the common gradient length. The first term is exactly the corresponding normalized tangential trace at $x'$, and the remaining term has absolute value at most $Cz$. Finally, the tensor trace changes by at most $Cz$, by the $C^1$ bound on $Q$ and parallel transport. It follows that $$\bigl|\mathcal E_Q[\psi](x)
             -\mathcal E_Q[\phi](x')\bigr|\leq Cz.$$ The assumed support inequality at $x$ proves Equation <a href="#n3:domains:parallel-estimate" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:parallel-estimate">[n3:domains:parallel-estimate]</a>. There is no term containing $z|\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi|$. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-domains-weak-support"></a>
<div id="n3:domains:weak-support" class="lemma">

**Lemma 18** (A smooth enclosure from weak supports). *Let $N$ be a smooth compact connected three-manifold with boundary $\Gamma_-\sqcup\Gamma_+$, where $\Gamma_+$ is nonempty and $\Gamma_-$ may be empty. Let $D$ be a nonempty closed subset which contains a relative collar of $\Gamma_-$ when that boundary is prescribed, and stays a positive distance from $\Gamma_+$. Suppose its interior frontier has exterior-support expansion at most $c$ for a smooth tensor $Q$.*

<a id="n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion"></a>
*For every $c'>c$ such that $\Theta_Q(\Gamma_+)>c'$ with its normal out of $N$, there is a smooth bounding domain $E$ containing $D$ in its relative interior, containing the required inner collar, and avoiding $\Gamma_+$, whose free boundary satisfies $$\label{n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion}
 \Theta_Q(\partial E\setminus\Gamma_-)=c'.$$ Its boundary and the domain may be disconnected. In particular $D$ is contained in the closed total trapped region at any such larger threshold. No regularity or positive-thickness assumption on $D$ is required.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-domains-weak-support"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-domains-weak-support</summary>

<a id="n3:domains:band-gap"></a>
*Proof.* All distance neighborhoods in this proof are relative to $N$. Since $D$ contains a collar of $\Gamma_-$ and avoids $\Gamma_+$, their new frontiers, at sufficiently small radii, lie in a compact subset of the interior. A minimizing segment ending on a new frontier has its nearest point on the interior frontier of $D$; it cannot start on $\Gamma_-$ because its covered collar has fixed positive width. Thus the proof of Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:parallel-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:parallel-support">17</a> applies unchanged. Choose $\beta>0$ so small that its conclusion holds for $0<z\leq\beta$, all these frontiers avoid the prescribed boundary, and $$\label{n3:domains:band-gap}
 c+C\beta<c'.$$

<a id="n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood"></a>
We first construct a smooth inner enclosure without imposing any expansion bound on it. Smoothly approximate the continuous distance function $d_D=\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,D)$ on $N$ uniformly, with error less than $\beta/32$, using a finite coordinate cover, mollification, and a partition of unity. Choose a regular value in $(\beta/3,\beta/2)$ of the resulting smooth function. Its sublevel set $U$ has smooth interior boundary and, for example, satisfies $$\label{n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood}
 D_{\beta/4}\subset U\subset D_{3\beta/4}.$$ The boundary $\Gamma_-$ is contained in its relative interior and $\Gamma_+$ is excluded. If a component of $N\setminus\overline U$ meets no component of $\Gamma_+$, fill it. This only deletes components of the smooth free boundary. After this filling the second inclusion in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood">[n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood]</a> need not hold for its interior, but every remaining free boundary component still lies in the indicated thin neighborhood, and the first inclusion still holds.

<a id="n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion"></a>
Choose $\eta\in C^\infty(N)$, $0\leq\eta\leq1$, equal to one on that free boundary and supported in $\{d_D<\beta\}$. Its existence uses the positive separation between this compact smooth boundary and the closed set $\{d_D\geq\beta\}$; it requires no smoothness of $d_D$. For a sufficiently large finite constant $A$, the tensor <a id="n3:domains:modified-tensor"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:modified-tensor}
 Q_A=Q-\tfrac12(c'+A\eta)g$$ makes the free boundary of $U$ a strictly negative inner barrier: $$\Theta_{Q_A}(\partial U)
       =\Theta_Q(\partial U)-c'-A<0.$$ All prescribed outer faces remain strictly positive for $Q_A$, because $\eta=0$ there and their original expansion exceeds $c'$. Apply the barrier part of Theorem <a href="#n3:domains:region-theorem" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:region-theorem">13</a> on each component of $N\setminus\overline U$. Each meets $\Gamma_+$ by the filling step and has nonempty inner boundary by connectedness of $N$ and $U\ne\varnothing$. We obtain smooth MOTSs $\Sigma$ bounding a domain $E$ which contains $\overline U$ and avoids $\Gamma_+$. They satisfy, with their normal out of $E$, $$\label{n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion}
 \Theta_Q(\Sigma)=c'+A\eta\geq c'.$$

We claim $\Sigma$ misses $\{d_D<\beta\}$. Otherwise set $z=\min_{\Sigma}d_D<\beta$. The first inclusion in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood">[n3:domains:initial-smooth-neighborhood]</a> gives $z\geq\beta/4>0$. Moreover $D_z$ lies on the inner side of $\Sigma$. To see this directly, if $d_D(y)<z$, a shortest path from $y$ to $D$ of length less than $z$ cannot cross $\Sigma$: such a crossing would have distance from $D$ less than $z$. Since $D\subset E$, the whole path and $y$ lie in $E$. Closure gives $D_z\subset\overline E$.

At a point attaining the minimum, a defining function for the smooth boundary $\Sigma$ is therefore an exterior support to $D_z$, with the same outward normal as in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion">[n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion]</a>. The parallel support bound and Equation <a href="#n3:domains:band-gap" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:band-gap">[n3:domains:band-gap]</a> imply $$\Theta_Q(\Sigma)\leq c+Cz<c',$$ contradicting Equation <a href="#n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion">[n3:domains:modified-mots-expansion]</a>. This excludes the entire modification range, so $\eta=0$ on $\Sigma$ and proves Equation <a href="#n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion">[n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion]</a>. The contained $D_{\beta/4}$ gives strict enclosure of $D$. If desired, fill any remaining complementary components which meet no designated outer face; this deletes smooth boundary components and preserves all stated properties. ◻

</details>

For an exterior, truncate by a distant sphere that is strict at the larger threshold. In the black construction, $\mathcal B$ already contains the original inner collar. In the white construction there is no required inner boundary, and the black faces belong to $\Gamma_+$. The later applications therefore need compact avoidance of the foreign faces; they need no boundary regularity of the weak set. Empty weak sets can be omitted.

<a id="pm-h-23"></a>
###### Small offsets and the prepared domain

<a id="stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain"></a>
<div id="n3:domains:prepared-domain" class="proposition">

**Proposition 19** (Prepared domain). *The thresholds and the domain above can be chosen with the following properties. The numbers $c_b,c_w<0$ are right-continuity points of their respective full maximal-region families. The boundary of $\Omega$ consists of the faces in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:face-expansions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:face-expansions">[n3:domains:face-expansions]</a>, has disjoint smooth outward leaf collars as in Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:stable-collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:stable-collar">15</a>, and preserves the enclosing-area lower bound in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:inherited-area" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:inherited-area">[n3:domains:inherited-area]</a>.*

<a id="n3:domains:offset-smallness"></a>
*There are a smooth compactly supported function $C$ on $\Omega$, constants $C_b\geq0$, $C_w\leq0$, and positive constants $k_B$ on its face collars such that <a id="n3:domains:offset-collars"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:offset-collars}
 \begin{aligned}
  C_w\leq C\leq C_b,&\qquad
  C=C_b-k_Bs&&\text{in a black collar near }B_b,\\
  &\qquad C=C_w+k_Bs&&\text{in a white collar near }B_w.
 \end{aligned}$$ For an absent type, its corresponding constant is simply a bound. Set <a id="n3:domains:assigned-heights"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:assigned-heights}
 b_-=c_b-C_b<0,
 \qquad b_+=-c_w-C_w>0.$$ There is a smooth positive function $\rho$, equal to a positive constant times $r^{-4}$ on the far end and satisfying symbol derivative bounds there, such that, for every $h\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$\label{n3:domains:offset-smallness}
 |(h+C)\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K|+|\nabla C|+\rho
      \leq\tfrac12\mathfrak m
 \quad\hbox{everywhere on }\Omega.$$ The thresholds, collars, offset, and $\rho$ are fixed before the deformation parameters are chosen. After fixing the thresholds and collars, the offset and its first derivatives can be made arbitrarily small.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain</summary>

*Proof.* The large-sphere comparison above confines all negative-threshold regions to a fixed compact set, independently of how close the thresholds are to zero. Choose a slightly larger compact set $\mathcal K$ containing this range and $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}K$ in its interior. Let $$m_0=\min_{\mathcal K}\mathfrak m>0,
 \qquad T_0=\sup_{\mathcal K}|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K|.$$ First restrict both negative thresholds to an interval so close to zero that $$\max\{|c_b|,|c_w|\}\,T_0<m_0/8,$$ while retaining Equation <a href="#n3:domains:black-interval" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:black-interval">[n3:domains:black-interval]</a>. Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:right-continuity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:right-continuity">14</a> allows the required successive choices in that interval. Construct the two regions, select $\Omega$, and fix their disjoint collars inside $\mathcal K$ as above. All ensuing constants may depend on these fixed choices.

Here is an explicit offset construction. On each collar choose a smooth nonincreasing cutoff $\chi(s)$, equal to one near $s=0$ and zero near the collar’s far end. Choose $\kappa_B>0$ so that $1-\kappa_Bs>0$ throughout that collar. For a common amplitude $a>0$, define the contribution of a black collar to be $a\chi(s)(1-\kappa_Bs)$, and that of a white collar to be $-a\chi(s)(1-\kappa_Bs)$. Extend by zero outside the disjoint collars and sum. This produces a smooth function on the manifold with boundary $\Omega$, supported in $\mathcal K$, with $C_b=a$, $C_w=-a$, and $k_B=a\kappa_B$ on the respective collars. These remain valid bounds when a type is absent. Its $C^1$ norm tends to zero with $a$, even though the collar widths have already been fixed.

For $h\in[b_-,b_+]$ and $C\in[C_w,C_b]$, $$|h+C|\leq\max\{|c_b|,|c_w|\}+C_b-C_w.$$ Choose $a$ so small that $(C_b-C_w)T_0+\|\nabla C\|_\infty<m_0/8$. The first two terms of Equation <a href="#n3:domains:offset-smallness" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:offset-smallness">[n3:domains:offset-smallness]</a> are then at most $m_0/4$ on $\mathcal K$ and vanish outside $\mathcal K$. Finally take a fixed smooth positive weight equal to $r^{-4}$ far out and multiply it by a sufficiently small positive constant. The end lower bound for $\mathfrak m$ and $\delta<1$, together with compact positivity, allow the choice $\rho\leq\mathfrak m/4$ everywhere. This proves Equation <a href="#n3:domains:offset-smallness" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:offset-smallness">[n3:domains:offset-smallness]</a>. All remaining assertions were proved in constructing the regions and collars. ◻

</details>

At the assigned face heights the quantity $h+C$ consequently has the useful exact values <a id="n3:domains:compatible-face-values"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:compatible-face-values}
 \begin{aligned}
  h+C&=c_b=P_B+H&&\text{on }B_b\text{ when }h=b_-,\\
  h+C&=-c_w=P_B-H&&\text{on }B_w\text{ when }h=b_+.
 \end{aligned}$$ These identities determine the deformation’s boundary signs. Right-continuity and Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:weak-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:weak-support">18</a> will exclude limiting sublevel sets away from the corresponding full trapped regions.

<a id="pm-h-24"></a>
##### The elliptic deformation and exclusion of the floor

<a id="n3:deformation:face-thresholds"></a>
We define the coupled system, derive its scalar-curvature identity, and choose a continuation path along which the conformal factor cannot touch its lower bound. We use the fixed data of Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">19</a>. Thus $\Omega$ has one controlled asymptotically flat end, $K$ is compactly supported, and its compact boundary $B=B_b\cup B_w$ consists of black and white faces. Either type may be absent. The normal $\nu$ points into $\Omega$, and $$H=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_B\nu,\qquad P_B=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_BK.$$ The numbers $b_-<0<b_+$, the smooth compactly supported offset $C$, and the positive function $\rho=O(r^{-4})$ are fixed as in that proposition. In particular, $$\label{n3:deformation:face-thresholds}
 b_-+C=P_B+H\ \hbox{on }B_b,\qquad
 b_++C=P_B-H\ \hbox{on }B_w.$$ All compact sets and geometric constants in this section are fixed after this preparation. Extend the end radius to a smooth function on $\overline\Omega$ bounded below by one. Write $\Omega_R$ for the large spherical truncations and $S_R$ for their outer boundary.

A *polynomial constant* is bounded by $C(1+n)^N$, with $C,N$ depending on the prepared data and fixed auxiliary profiles, but not on $R$, the homotopy parameter, or the solution. Constants permitted to depend arbitrarily on fixed $n$ will be identified explicitly. First fix $0<\epsilon<1$, then choose $n$ sufficiently large, and finally require $R\ge R_{\min}(n,\epsilon)$. We always take $n\ge4$ and $n>2/\epsilon$.

<a id="n3:deformation:variables"></a>
###### Variables and equations

Choose a smooth nonincreasing $\vartheta:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ equal to one on $(-\infty,0]$ and zero on $[1,\infty)$. Define <a id="n3:deformation:l-profile"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:l-profile}
 \begin{gathered}
 p(t)=n\vartheta(nt),\qquad
 l(t)=\exp\left(\int_0^t p(s)\,\mathrm ds\right),\\
 L(t)=l(t)e^{2t},\qquad p_L=p+2.
 \end{gathered}$$ Thus $l(0)=1$, $l(t)=e^{nt}$ for $t\le0$, and $l$ is constant for $t\ge1/n$. Derivatives of $p$ of every fixed order are polynomially bounded. Set <a id="n3:deformation:small-parameters"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:small-parameters}
 \ell=e^{-\epsilon n},\qquad \tau=\ell^{3/2}.$$ Whenever $t\ge-\epsilon$, one has $\ell\le l(t)\le e$.

<a id="n3:deformation:axial-matrices"></a>
For a function $f$, set <a id="n3:deformation:basic-variables"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:basic-variables}
 \begin{gathered}
 \sigma=|\nabla f|,\quad D=1+l^2\sigma^2,\quad d=D^{-1},\\
 a=l\sigma/\sqrt D,\quad v=a^2=1-d,\quad
 w=l\nabla f/\sqrt D,\quad \chi=4d/(4+pv),\\
 Z=t+\tfrac18\log D,\quad u=L\sqrt D,\quad U=l\sqrt D,\quad h=\tau f.
 \end{gathered}$$ Derivatives and contractions refer to $g$ unless indicated otherwise. At $\sigma>0$, write $e=\nabla f/\sigma$ and $A_j=I+(j-1)e\otimes e$. The matrices used below have the direction-free expressions $$\label{n3:deformation:axial-matrices}
 A_d=I-w\otimes w,\qquad
 A_\chi=I-\frac{p+4}{4+pv}w\otimes w.$$ Vectors and covectors are identified with $g$.

<a id="n3:deformation:trace"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:flux"></a>
The unknowns will be $(f,Z)$. For fixed $\nabla f$, $\partial Z/\partial t=1+pv/4>0$, and its defining expression tends to $-\infty$ and $+\infty$ at the two ends of the $t$-axis. It therefore defines a unique smooth $t=t(Z,\nabla f)$ for all inputs, without a floor assumption. The formulas above are smooth at $\nabla f=0$, and $0<\chi\le d\le1$ for finite inputs. Define <a id="n3:deformation:metrics"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:metrics}
 \bar g=g+l^2\,\mathrm df^2,\qquad \hat g=e^{4t}\bar g,\qquad
 H^f=\frac l{\sqrt D}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}f,\qquad S=K+H^f.$$ The original trace equation is $$\label{n3:deformation:trace}
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}S=F,\qquad F=h+C,$$ where $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_A S$ is contraction with the contravariant matrix $A$. Along the continuation path we will specify modified right sides $F$. The full flux is $$\label{n3:deformation:flux}
 V=uA_\chi\bigl(4\nabla Z+K(w,\cdot)\bigr).$$ At $S_R$ prescribe $f=Z=0$. Initially the inner Dirichlet values are $h=b_-$ on $B_b$ and $h=b_+$ on $B_w$.

<a id="pm-h-26"></a>
###### The exact scalar-curvature identity

The next identity separates the original constraint densities, a nonnegative quadratic term, and a divergence. The second equation will prescribe that divergence so that the deformed metric has nonnegative scalar curvature.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-identity"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:identity" class="proposition">

<a id="n3:deformation:quadratic-term"></a>
**Proposition 20** (Deformation identity). *Let $f,t$ be smooth and $F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}(K+H^f)$. At $\sigma>0$ decompose $S$ relative to $\mathbb Re\oplus e^\perp$: $$T=S|_{e^\perp\times e^\perp},\quad
 M=S(e,\cdot)|_{e^\perp},\quad q=S(e,e),\quad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}T=F-\chi q.$$ Then <a id="n3:deformation:scalar-identity"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:scalar-identity}
 \begin{split}
 \tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g}
 ={}&8\pi(\mu+J(w))+\mathcal T
       +w(F)-F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V,
 \end{split}$$ where $$\label{n3:deformation:quadratic-term}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2
 +(M+pa\nabla_\perp t)\cdot(M+(p+2)a\nabla_\perp t)\\
 &+4(p+1)|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2
   +(\chi-\chi^2/4)q^2+2(p+1)\chi qa\,\partial_e t\\
 &-\chi Fq/2+3F^2/4.
 \end{split}$$ After substituting $F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}S$, this expression extends smoothly across $\sigma=0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-identity"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-identity</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:auxiliary-k"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:stationary-scalar"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:bar-laplacian"></a>
*Proof.* Introduce an auxiliary coordinate $s_0$ and the stationary Lorentz metric $${\bf g}=-l^2(\,\mathrm ds_0-\,\mathrm df)^2+\bar g
       =-U^2\,\mathrm ds_0^2+g(\,\mathrm dx+\beta\,\mathrm ds_0,\,\mathrm dx+\beta\,\mathrm ds_0),
 \qquad \beta=l^2\nabla f=Uw.$$ Its $s_0$-slices have future normal $N_0=(\partial_{s_0}-\beta)/U$ and second fundamental form $$\label{n3:deformation:auxiliary-k}
 k=-\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{sym}}\nabla\beta}{U}
   =-H^f-p(\,\mathrm dt\otimes w^\flat+w^\flat\otimes\,\mathrm dt).$$ Write $\theta=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}k$ and, for symmetric tensors, put $$\mathscr B(A,B)=\langle A,B\rangle-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}A)(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}B),\qquad
 P_A=A-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}A)g,\qquad Q=K-k.$$ The normal expansion equation and contracted Gauss equation are $$\begin{split}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\bf g}(N_0,N_0)&=-N_0(\theta)-|k|^2+U^{-1}\Delta U,\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g&=\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bf g}+2\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\bf g}(N_0,N_0)+|k|^2-\theta^2.
 \end{split}$$ Consequently $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bf g}=\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g+|k|^2+\theta^2+
2N_0(\theta)-2U^{-1}\Delta U$. Stationarity gives $UN_0(\theta)=-\beta(\theta)$, and $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\beta=-U\theta$ follows from <a href="#n3:deformation:auxiliary-k" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:auxiliary-k">[n3:deformation:auxiliary-k]</a>. Thus $$\label{n3:deformation:stationary-scalar}
 U\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bf g}
 =U\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g+\mathscr B(k,k)\bigr)
   -2\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(\nabla U+\theta\beta).$$ In the coordinates $s_0-f$ the same metric is a static warped product. Its mixed Christoffel symbols are $\mathbf{\Gamma}^{s}_{is}=\partial_i\log l$ and $\mathbf{\Gamma}^{i}_{ss}=l\bar\nabla^il$; contraction gives $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bf g}=\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bar g}-2l^{-1}\bar\Delta l$. Since $\bar g^{-1}=A_d$ and $\,\mathrm dV_{\bar g}=(U/l)\,\mathrm dV_g$, $$\label{n3:deformation:bar-laplacian}
 \bar\Delta\phi=\frac lU\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\left(\frac Ul A_d\nabla\phi\right).$$ Direct differentiation of $U$ and <a href="#n3:deformation:auxiliary-k" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:auxiliary-k">[n3:deformation:auxiliary-k]</a> gives $$\nabla U-\frac Ul A_d\nabla l=-k(\beta,\cdot).$$ In fact both sides equal $$\frac{l^4}{U}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}f(\nabla f,\cdot)
 +\frac{l^3}{U}\bigl[|\nabla f|^2\,\mathrm dl
                       +(\nabla f)(l)\,\mathrm df\bigr],$$ as follows by differentiating $U^2=l^2+l^4|\nabla f|^2$. Substitution in <a href="#n3:deformation:stationary-scalar" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:stationary-scalar">[n3:deformation:stationary-scalar]</a> yields $$U\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bar g}
 =U\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g+\mathscr B(k,k)\bigr)+2\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(P_k\beta).$$ The constraints read $16\pi\mu=\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-\mathscr B(K,K)$ and $8\pi J=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}P_K$. Using $P_K:\nabla\beta=-U\mathscr B(K,k)$, expansion therefore gives <a id="n3:deformation:unweighted-identity"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:unweighted-identity}
 U\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bar g}
 =U[16\pi(\mu+J(w))+\mathscr B(Q,Q)]-2\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(P_Q\beta).$$ Indeed the derivative of $P_K$ cancels its term in $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(P_K\beta)$, and $\mathscr B(Q,Q)+2\mathscr B(K,k)=\mathscr B(K,K)+\mathscr B(k,k)$.

<a id="n3:deformation:pre-flux"></a>
The three-dimensional conformal formula is $$\tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g}
 =\tfrac12\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\bar g}-4\bar\Delta t-4|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2.$$ For $Y=P_Qw$, replacing $U$ by $u=e^{2t}U$ gives $-U^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(UY)=-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uY)+2Y(t)$. Since $u/(U/l)=L$, Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:bar-laplacian" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:bar-laplacian">[n3:deformation:bar-laplacian]</a> similarly gives $$-4\bar\Delta t-4|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2
 =-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(4uA_d\nabla t)+4(p+1)|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2.$$ Before the flux modification, the scalar-curvature expression is $$\label{n3:deformation:pre-flux}
 \begin{split}
 8\pi(\mu+J(w))+\tfrac12\mathscr B(Q,Q)
 +2P_Q(w,\nabla t)+4(p+1)|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2\\
 -u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\bigl(u(P_Qw+4A_d\nabla t)\bigr).
 \end{split}$$

<a id="n3:deformation:Z-differential"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:quadratic-invariant"></a>
At $\sigma>0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:Z-differential}
 4\,\mathrm dZ=(4+pv)\,\mathrm dt+v\,\mathrm d\log\sigma.$$ Write $x=\partial_e t$ and $y=\nabla_\perp t$. The blocks of $Q$ are $$\begin{gathered}
 Q_{\perp\perp}=T,\qquad Q_{e\perp}=M+pay,\qquad Q_{ee}=q+2pax,\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}Q=F+(1-\chi)q+2pax.
 \end{gathered}$$ Hence $(P_Qw)_\perp=a(M+pay)$ and $(P_Qw)_e=a(\chi q-F)$. Together with $aH^f(e,\cdot)=v\,\mathrm d\log\sigma$, Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:Z-differential" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:Z-differential">[n3:deformation:Z-differential]</a> proves component by component <a id="n3:deformation:flux-rewrite"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:flux-rewrite}
 V/u=P_Qw+4A_d\nabla t+wF.$$ Also $uw=e^{2t}l^2\nabla f$, so <a id="n3:deformation:uw-divergence"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:uw-divergence}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uw)/u
 =F+(1-\chi)q-\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K+2(p+1)ax.$$ Replacing the flux in <a href="#n3:deformation:pre-flux" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:pre-flux">[n3:deformation:pre-flux]</a> adds $w(F)+F\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uw)/u$. The remaining quadratic expression is $$\label{n3:deformation:quadratic-invariant}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12\mathscr B(Q,Q)+2P_Q(w,\nabla t)
                  +4(p+1)|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2\\
 &+F\left[F+\frac{p+4}{4+pv}S(w,w)+2(p+1)w(t)\right].
 \end{split}$$ Here $(1-\chi)q=(p+4)S(w,w)/(4+pv)$, which gives a smooth formula at $w=0$.

For the explicit coefficients, substitute $|T|^2=|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+(F-\chi q)^2/2$ in $\mathscr B(Q,Q)/2$. The transverse terms become $(M+pay)\cdot(M+(p+2)ay)$. The coefficients of $q^2,Fq,F^2$ are respectively $\chi-\chi^2/4,-\chi/2,3/4$. The $qx$ coefficient is $2(p+1)\chi a$, the $Fx$ terms cancel, and the remaining $x^2$ term is $4(p+1)dx^2$. These are the terms in <a href="#n3:deformation:quadratic-term" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:quadratic-term">[n3:deformation:quadratic-term]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:coercivity" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:coercive-estimate"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:floor-norm"></a>
**Lemma 21** (Polynomial coercivity). *The expression $\mathcal T$ is nonnegative. For $0\le p\le n$, $$\label{n3:deformation:coercive-estimate}
 |\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2+|T|^2+|M|^2+dq^2+F^2
 \le C(1+n)^N\mathcal T$$ with universal $C,N$. At $\,\mathrm dt=0$ there is the stronger comparison, uniform in $p,d$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-norm}
 c\bigl(|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+|M|^2+\chi q^2+F^2\bigr)
 \le\mathcal T
 \le C\bigl(|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+|M|^2+\chi q^2+F^2\bigr).$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:square-completion"></a>
*Proof.* With $x=\partial_e t$ and $y=\nabla_\perp t$, exact completion gives $$\label{n3:deformation:square-completion}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2
 +|M+(p+1)ay|^2+[4(p+1)-v]|y|^2\\
 &+4(p+1)d\left(x+\frac{\chi aq}{4d}\right)^2\\
 &+\tfrac34\left(F-\frac{\chi q}{3}\right)^2
 +\frac{4d(9-d)}{3(4+pv)^2}q^2.
 \end{split}$$ Completing first in $x$ leaves $3\chi q^2/(4+pv)$; completing next in $F$ leaves $3\chi/(4+pv)-\chi^2/12=4d(9-d)/[3(4+pv)^2]$. The latter coefficient is at least $32d/[3(4+n)^2]$. It controls $dq^2$ polynomially. The $F$-square then controls $F^2$, since $\chi^2q^2\le dq^2$. The transverse gradient coefficient is at least three, and the shifted $M$-square controls $M$ with an additional factor $(1+n)^2$. The squared $d$-norm of the shift in the $x$-square is $\chi^2vq^2/(16d)\le dq^2/16$, so it also controls $dx^2$. Finally $|T|^2=|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+(F-\chi q)^2/2$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:coercive-estimate" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:coercive-estimate">[n3:deformation:coercive-estimate]</a>. If $\,\mathrm dt=0$, the sole cross term is $-\chi Fq/2$. Using $|\chi Fq|/2\le\chi q^2/4+\chi F^2/4$ and $0<\chi\le1$ proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:boundary-identity" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:boundary"></a>
**Lemma 22** (Boundary identity). *On a face where $f$ is constant, $$\label{n3:deformation:boundary}
 V_\nu/u=d(H+4\partial_\nu t)-H+w_\nu(F-P_B).$$ Its mean curvature in $\hat g$, with normal into $\Omega$, is $e^{-2t}\sqrt d\,(H+4\partial_\nu t)$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity</summary>

*Proof.* The tangential Hessian is $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}f|_{TB}=(\partial_\nu f)\operatorname{II}_g$. Thus $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp H^f=w_\nu H$ and $\chi q=F-P_B-w_\nu H$. The normal component of <a href="#n3:deformation:flux" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:flux">[n3:deformation:flux]</a>, using <a href="#n3:deformation:Z-differential" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:Z-differential">[n3:deformation:Z-differential]</a>, is $$V_\nu/u=4d\partial_\nu t+\chi w_\nu q
        =4d\partial_\nu t+w_\nu(F-P_B)-vH.$$ The $\bar g$-normal is $\sqrt d\,\nu$. Its mean curvature is $\sqrt d\,H$, because the tangential metric is unchanged and its normal first variation is multiplied by $\sqrt d$. The conformal mean-curvature formula gives the asserted mean curvature for $\hat g$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-27"></a>
###### The source, boundary condition, and continuation path

We now prescribe the divergence and inner flux. For the original system, the source is chosen to give the deformed metric nonnegative scalar curvature. A penalty near the lower bound will exclude contact with that bound along the continuation path.

<a id="n3:deformation:source"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:original-second-equation"></a>
Choose $3/4<\gamma<1$ and fixed positive smooth weights $$\rho_0\asymp r^{-4},\qquad \rho_1\asymp r^{-2\gamma},$$ with differentiated end bounds. Let $m:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ be smooth, equal to one on $(-\infty,0]$ and zero on $[1,\infty)$, and set $$m_0(t)=m(n(t+\epsilon)),\qquad
 \mathcal P=C_n(\rho_0+v\rho_1).$$ The positive $\delta_0$ is fixed independently of $n,R$ in Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor">28</a>; thereafter $C_n$ is a sufficiently large polynomial constant. Define $$\label{n3:deformation:source}
 \Xi=\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho+\delta_0\tau a\sigma-m_0(t)\mathcal P.$$ Choose a smooth face function $N_B>1+\sup_B|H|$. The original second equation and its inner condition are $$\label{n3:deformation:original-second-equation}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}V=u\Xi,\qquad V_\nu/u=-H+w_\nu(F-P_B)-N_Bd.$$ Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:boundary-identity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:boundary-identity">22</a> gives $H+4\partial_\nu t=-N_B$. Only $-\epsilon\le t\le-\epsilon+1/n$ is penalized in the admissible range. Since $n>2/\epsilon$, this band has negative $t$, and <a id="n3:deformation:penalty-band"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:penalty-band}
 \ell\le l\le e\ell,\qquad c\ell\le L\le C\ell
 \quad\hbox{on the admissible penalty band}.$$ The latter constants can be uniform for $0<\epsilon<1$.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:homotopy" class="proposition">

**Proposition 23** (Specified homotopy). *There is a continuous piecewise smooth family of systems indexed by $s\in[0,4]$, beginning at <a href="#n3:deformation:trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:trace">[n3:deformation:trace]</a>, <a href="#n3:deformation:original-second-equation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:original-second-equation">[n3:deformation:original-second-equation]</a> and the original Dirichlet values, and ending at $f=0$ and the scalar problem with zero source and zero inner conormal flux. Throughout its first three stages the source is <a href="#n3:deformation:source" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:source">[n3:deformation:source]</a>, with $\mathcal T$ evaluated using the actual trace $F$. Each trace equation has right-side derivative at least one in $h$, with $x,Z,\nabla f$ fixed.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary"></a>
*Proof.* Fix a smooth $j:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ which vanishes for $t\le0$ and equals one for $t\ge1$. For $0\le\lambda\le1$ put $$V_\lambda=uA_\chi(4\nabla Z+\lambda K(w,\cdot)),\qquad
 \mathcal B=-H+w_\nu(F-P_B)-N_Bd.$$ Before the last stage use the boundary condition $$\label{n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary}
 \begin{split}
 (V_\lambda)_\nu/u
 ={}&[1-(1-\lambda)j(t)]\\
 &\cdot[\mathcal B-(1-\lambda)(A_\chi K(w,\cdot))_\nu].
 \end{split}$$ Outer values remain $f=Z=0$ throughout.

We specify two smooth collar modifications. Let $\nu_s=\nabla s/|\nabla s|$ be the outward unit normal to a collar leaf; the leaf coordinate $s$ here is local and is separate from the homotopy parameter. Choose disjoint collar cutoffs equal to one at the faces. Take $\eta>0$ so small that $b_-+3\eta<b_+$. A black contribution to $D_0(x,w,h)$ is a negative constant times a collar cutoff, times a smooth directional cutoff supported where $w\cdot\nu_s<-1/2$ and equal to one at $-1$, times a nonincreasing height cutoff equal to one below $b_-+\eta$ and zero above $b_-+2\eta$. A white contribution has positive sign, its directional cutoff supported where $w\cdot\nu_s>1/2$ and equal to one at $1$, and a nondecreasing height cutoff equal to zero below $b_+-2\eta$ and one above $b_+-\eta$. Decrease $\eta$ to separate these ranges. Their sum $D_0$ is smooth, bounded, supported in the collars, and nondecreasing in $h$. It is nonpositive for $h\le b_-+\eta$, nonnegative for $h\ge b_+-\eta$, and vanishes on black outward and white inward directions, for every length $0\le|w|\le1$.

<a id="n3:deformation:directional-barriers"></a>
Choose the magnitudes larger than $2\sup_B|H|+1$. Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:face-thresholds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:face-thresholds">[n3:deformation:face-thresholds]</a> then gives, for $F=h+C+D_0$ at the assigned boundary height $b=b_\pm$, $$\label{n3:deformation:directional-barriers}
 F(x,+\nu,b)\ge P_B+H,\qquad F(x,-\nu,b)\le P_B-H.$$ These are limiting directional evaluations at $a=1,\chi=0$. The compatible direction has equality; $D_0$ corrects the other one. Its derivatives on bounded height ranges are independent of $n$. Choose a smooth compactly supported extension $b(x)$, constant equal to $b_\pm$ on each smaller collar. On these collars let $D_1(x,w)=A_1w\cdot\nu_s$, extended by a collar cutoff, with $A_1>\sup_B|H|+1$. Then $D_1(x,0)=0$ and $D_1(x,\pm\nu)=\pm A_1$ on $B$.

The four stages are the following.

1.  For $0\le s\le1$, set $\lambda=1-s$, keep $F=h+C$ and $h|_B=b$, and use $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V_\lambda=u\Xi$ and <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary">[n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary]</a>.

2.  For $1\le s\le2$, set $\lambda=0$, $\alpha=s-1$, retain $h|_B=b$, and replace the trace right side by $F=h+C+\alpha D_0(x,w,h)$. Keep the same scalar equation and boundary prescription.

3.  For $2\le s\le3$, set $\lambda=0$, $\zeta=s-2$, prescribe $h|_B=(1-\zeta)b$, and use <a id="n3:deformation:interpolation-trace"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:interpolation-trace}
     \begin{split}
     F={}&h+(1-\zeta)[C+D_0(x,w,h+\zeta b(x))]\\
        &+\zeta[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}K+D_1(x,w)].
     \end{split}$$ Keep the same scalar equation and boundary prescription. At a face, $h+\zeta b=b$. The value at $w=\pm\nu$ is the convex combination of the preceding directional value and $P_B+D_1(x,\pm\nu)$, so <a href="#n3:deformation:directional-barriers" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:directional-barriers">[n3:deformation:directional-barriers]</a> persists.

4.  For $3\le s\le4$, retain the trace problem at $\zeta=1$ and multiply both $\Xi$ and the right side of <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary">[n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary]</a> by $\eta_s=4-s$.

The prescriptions agree at the common endpoints. Their $h$-derivatives are $1$, $1+\alpha\partial_hD_0$, or $1+(1-\zeta)\partial_hD_0$, all at least one.

At $\zeta=1$ the trace equation is $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}H^f=h+D_1(x,w)$ with zero Dirichlet values. At a positive interior maximum of $f$, one has $w=0$, $A_\chi=I$, $D_1=0$, and $l\Delta f=\tau f>0$, a contradiction. A negative minimum is excluded in the same way. Thus $f=0$ and $t=Z$ in the last stage. At $s=4$ the remaining equation is $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(4L(Z)\nabla Z)=0$, with zero inner conormal flux and $Z=0$ on $S_R$. Multiplication by $Z$ and integration give $Z=0$. For the fixed-point construction in Section 6, the last map therefore has output identically zero. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-28"></a>
###### Elementary height and end barriers

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-height"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:height" class="lemma">

**Lemma 24** (Height control). *Every smooth trace solution in Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">23</a> satisfies $|h|\le C_0$, independently of $n,R$, the homotopy parameter, and the input $Z$. Its actual right side satisfies $|F|\le C_F$ with the same independence.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-height"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-height</summary>

*Proof.* The collar modifications vanish at $w=0$. At an interior extremum the trace equation reads either $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K+l\Delta f=h+C$ or $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K+l\Delta f=h+(1-\zeta)C+\zeta\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K$. The maximum and minimum inequalities bound $h$ by fixed bounds for $|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K|+|C|$. Boundary values range between $b_-,0,b_+$. This proves the height bound without using the floor. Boundedness of $D_0,D_1$ and $|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}K|\le3|K|$ proves the assertion for $F$. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-end-height"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:end-height" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:outer-gradient"></a>
**Lemma 25** (End height and outer boundary). *There are $r_0,C>0$, independent of $n,R$ and the homotopy parameter, such that for $R\ge2r_0$, <a id="n3:deformation:end-height-estimate"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:end-height-estimate}
 |h|\le C(r^{-\gamma}-R^{-\gamma})\quad(r_0\le r\le R).$$ In particular, $$\label{n3:deformation:outer-gradient}
 |\nabla f|\le C R^{-1-\gamma}/\tau\quad\hbox{on }S_R.$$ For fixed $\epsilon,n$, a sufficiently large lower bound for $R$ gives $t>-\epsilon$ on $S_R$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-end-height"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-end-height</summary>

*Proof.* Take $r_0$ outside the supports of $K,C,D_0,D_1$. There $F=h$ in the first three stages, and $h=0$ in the last one. For $\psi=r^{-\gamma}$, with axis $\nabla\psi/|\nabla\psi|$, the controlled end gives, uniformly for $0<\chi\le1$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\psi
 =\gamma((\gamma+1)\chi-2)r^{-\gamma-2}
      +O(r^{-\gamma-3})<0$$ after enlarging $r_0$. At a comparison contact, coefficients use the given $Z$ and the common gradient of test and solution. The positive factor $l/(\tau\sqrt D)$ preserves this sign. Height monotonicity therefore makes $C(\psi-R^{-\gamma})$ an upper barrier and its negative a lower barrier. Choose $C$ to dominate $C_0$ on $r=r_0$ for every $R\ge2r_0$. Differentiating at the common outer value gives <a href="#n3:deformation:outer-gradient" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:outer-gradient">[n3:deformation:outer-gradient]</a>; tangential derivatives there vanish.

At $S_R$, $Z=0$. The monotonicity of its defining expression implies $t>-\epsilon$ if $\ell^2|\nabla f|^2<e^{8\epsilon}-1$. It suffices to require $C^2\ell^2\tau^{-2}R^{-2-2\gamma}<e^{8\epsilon}-1$, which is a permissible lower bound depending on fixed $n,\epsilon$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-29"></a>
###### Exclusion of a contact with the floor

We exclude a proposed floor contact using the equations at that point. These estimates require neither an upper bound for $Z$ nor a bound for $|\nabla f|$.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:floor-curvature" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-gauss"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end"></a>
**Lemma 26** (Curvature at a minimum of $t$). *At an interior point where $\,\mathrm dt=0$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}t\ge0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-gauss}
 \tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g}
 \le \tfrac12\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)+\mathcal S(H^f),$$ where, for a symmetric tensor $A$, $$\label{n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal S(A)={}&\tfrac14(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A)^2
 -\tfrac12|A_{\perp\perp}^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2\\
 &+dA_{ee}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A-d|A_{e\perp}|^2.
 \end{split}$$ There are universal $c_*,\eta_*>0$ and polynomial constants $C_n$ such that, at $\,\mathrm dt=0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general}
 \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)
 \ge c_*\mathcal T-C_n(F^2+|K|^2).$$ If $K=0$, the more useful uniform estimate is $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end}
 \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)\ge c_*\mathcal T-C_n vF^2.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature</summary>

*Proof.* Consider the graph of $f$ in the Riemannian product with warped fiber $(\Omega\times\mathbb R,g+l^2\,\mathrm db_0^2)$. Its induced metric is $\bar g$. At $\,\mathrm dt=0$ one also has $\,\mathrm dl=0$, and its second fundamental form, up to orientation, is $H^f$. Write $E=l^{-1}\partial_{b_0}$. The graph unit normal is $\sqrt d\,E-ae$. The ambient curvature formulas at this point are $$\begin{gathered}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\mathrm{amb}}=\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-2\Delta l/l,\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathrm{amb}}|_{T\Omega}=\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g-\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}l/l,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathrm{amb}}(E,E)=-\Delta l/l,
 \end{gathered}$$ with zero mixed Ricci terms. Hence the ambient contribution to half the graph scalar curvature is $$\tfrac12\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)
      -v\,\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}l/l.$$ The last term is nonpositive: at $\,\mathrm dt=0$, $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}l=lp\,\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}t$ and $p\ge0$. The second-form contribution is $[(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{\bar g}H^f)^2-|H^f|_{\bar g}^2]/2$. Since the inverse graph metric is $A_d$, its expansion is exactly <a href="#n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic">[n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic]</a>. Finally the conformal contribution at this point is $-4\bar\Delta t\le0$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-gauss" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-gauss">[n3:deformation:floor-gauss]</a>.

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-difference"></a>
For the algebraic estimates we must retain the degenerate normal coefficient. First evaluate $\mathcal S$ on $S=K+H^f$, whose trace in the transverse plane is $F-\chi q$. Subtracting <a href="#n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic">[n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic]</a> from <a href="#n3:deformation:quadratic-term" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:quadratic-term">[n3:deformation:quadratic-term]</a> at $\,\mathrm dt=0$ gives $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-difference}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T-\mathcal S(S)
 ={}&|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+(1+d)|M|^2\\
 &+\chi(1+d-\chi/2)q^2-dFq+F^2/2.
 \end{split}$$ The normal coefficient is at least $\chi$, while $|dFq|\le\chi q^2/2+d^2F^2/(2\chi)$. Because $$d^2/\chi=d(4+pv)/4\le1+n/4,$$ Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> implies $\mathcal T-\mathcal S(S)\ge c\mathcal T-C(1+n)F^2$ with universal $c>0$.

To replace $S$ by $H^f=S-K$, polarize <a href="#n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic">[n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic]</a>. The difference is bounded by $$C|K|(|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|+|M|+|F|+d|q|)+C|K|^2.$$ Indeed the only extra normal product is $dq\,\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp K$; all remaining products involve transverse entries, $dM$, or $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp S=F-\chi q$. By <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> and $d/\sqrt\chi\le C\sqrt{1+n}$, this bound is at most $C\sqrt{1+n}|K|\sqrt{\mathcal T}+C|K|^2$. Young’s inequality absorbs a fixed small fraction of $\mathcal T$ and costs only $C(1+n)|K|^2$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general]</a>.

If $(1+p)v\le\eta_*$, then $d$ and $\chi$ are within $C\eta_*$ of one. At $d=\chi=1$ the normal block in <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-difference" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-difference">[n3:deformation:floor-difference]</a> is $3q^2/2-Fq+F^2/2$; its symmetric matrix has smallest eigenvalue $(2-\sqrt2)/2>0$. Choose $\eta_*>0$ small enough that its coefficients remain within half this spectral gap. The transverse coefficients are already bounded below. For $K=0$, Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> therefore gives $\mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)\ge c_*\mathcal T$ in this regime. In the remaining regime $v>\eta_* /(1+p)$, use <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general]</a> with $K=0$ and absorb $(1+n)F^2$ into $C(1+n)^2vF^2$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end]</a>. All formulas extend to $\sigma=0$ by their invariant expressions; there $d=\chi=1$ and the full quadratic expressions are independent of the temporary choice of axis. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:floor-errors" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower"></a>
**Lemma 27** (Homotopy errors at a floor contact). *There is a fixed compact set $\mathcal K\subset\overline\Omega$ containing the supports of $K,C,b,D_0,D_1$ such that, at an interior minimum $t=-\epsilon$ of a smooth solution in the first three stages, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}V_\lambda/u
 \ge 2\delta_0\mathcal T+\tau a\sigma
      -C(1+n)^N
       [\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}+v(\rho_0+\rho_1)].$$ Here $\delta_0>0$ can be fixed sufficiently small independently of $n,R$ and the homotopy parameter.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-w-control"></a>
*Proof.* At this contact $\,\mathrm dt=0$ and $p=n$ is locally constant as a function of $t$ near its value $-\epsilon$. Differentiating $w$ in an orthonormal frame gives <a id="n3:deformation:floor-w-derivative"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:floor-w-derivative}
 \nabla_iw_j=H^f_{ij}-w_jH^f_{ik}w^k.$$ In the $e$-frame the normal vector slot is multiplied by $d$. Equations <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> and $d/\sqrt\chi\le C\sqrt{1+n}$ therefore show $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-w-control}
 |\nabla w|\le C(1+n)^N(|K|+\sqrt{\mathcal T}).$$ No bound for the uncontracted normal Hessian is asserted.

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-F-control"></a>
Each first-three-stage right side can be written as a smooth function $F(x,w,h,p)$. Its $h$-derivative is at least one. On the bounded height range supplied by Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:height">24</a>, its explicit $x$- and $w$-derivatives are polynomially bounded and compactly supported, apart from the derivative of the term $h$. This follows directly from the fixed collar cutoffs and $A_\chi=I-(p+4)w\otimes w/(4+pv)$, whose denominator is at least four. For example its first $w$-derivatives on $|w|\le1$ are bounded by $C(1+n)^2$, and the other explicit modifications have bounds independent of $n$. Combining these bounds with <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-w-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-w-control">[n3:deformation:floor-w-control]</a> and Young’s inequality therefore produces a fixed finite power of $1+n$. Since $\nabla p=0$ at the contact and $w(h)=\tau a\sigma$, the chain rule and <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-w-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-w-control">[n3:deformation:floor-w-control]</a> give, for every fixed $\eta>0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-F-control}
 w(F)\ge\tau a\sigma-\eta\mathcal T
                 -C_\eta(1+n)^N\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}.$$ The dependence $D_0(x,w,h+\zeta b(x))$ only adds the fixed compact derivative of $b$ and does not change this conclusion.

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-flux-control"></a>
The omitted flux is $(1-\lambda)uA_\chi K(w,\cdot)$. Let $B_K=A_\chi K(w,\cdot)$. Its derivative is bounded by a polynomial constant times $1+\sqrt{\mathcal T}$ on $\mathcal K$, by <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-w-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-w-control">[n3:deformation:floor-w-control]</a>; derivatives of $p$ vanish. The weight term requires the contraction rather than a bound for $|\nabla\log u|$. At the contact, $$\nabla\log u=H^f(w,\cdot),\qquad
 \langle\nabla\log u,B_K\rangle
 =a^2\bigl(\chi H^f_{ee}K_{ee}
                    +H^f_{e\perp}\cdot K_{e\perp}\bigr).$$ This involves only $\chi H^f_{ee}$ and $H^f_{e\perp}$ and is controlled by <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a>. It follows that $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-flux-control}
 |\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uB_K)|/u
 \le\eta\mathcal T+C_\eta(1+n)^N\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}.$$

Combine the scalar identity with <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-gauss" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-gauss">[n3:deformation:floor-gauss]</a>. The difference $8\pi\mu-\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g/2$ equals $((\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K)^2-|K|^2)/2$ and is compactly supported; so is $J$. The term $F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K$ is compactly bounded by Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:height">24</a>. On $\mathcal K$, Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general]</a> therefore contributes $c_*\mathcal T-C(1+n)^N$. Outside $\mathcal K$, $K=0$, $F=h$, and <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end]</a> together with Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:end-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:end-height">25</a> gives $c_*\mathcal T-C(1+n)^Nv r^{-2\gamma}$. The remaining Ricci term is bounded below by $-C\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}-Cv r^{-3}$; enlarge $\mathcal K$ if necessary. Both end weights are bounded by a multiple of $\rho_0+\rho_1$. Finally subtract the omitted flux and use <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-F-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-F-control">[n3:deformation:floor-F-control]</a>–<a href="#n3:deformation:floor-flux-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-flux-control">[n3:deformation:floor-flux-control]</a>, choosing their two $\eta$’s with sum at most $c_*/2$. Fix $0<\delta_0<\min(c_*/4,1/4)$. Decreasing it slightly if necessary gives <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower">[n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-floor"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:floor" class="proposition">

**Proposition 28** (Floor exclusion). *Choose $\delta_0$ as in Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-errors" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-errors">27</a>. There is a polynomial choice $C_n=C(1+n)^N$ in the penalty such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and all $R\ge R_{\mathrm{floor}}(n,\epsilon)$, no smooth solution anywhere along Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">23</a> can satisfy $t\ge-\epsilon$ and attain $t=-\epsilon$. In particular every such admissible solution has $t>-\epsilon$ on $\overline{\Omega_R}$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-floor"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-floor</summary>

*Proof.* Choose $R_{\mathrm{floor}}$ to include the requirement of Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:end-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:end-height">25</a>. A floor contact cannot occur on $S_R$. In the first three stages, an inner contact has $j(t)=0$. Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary">[n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary]</a> then cancels the omitted flux on both sides and gives $V_\nu/u=\mathcal B$. Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:boundary">[n3:deformation:boundary]</a> forces $H+4\partial_\nu t=-N_B$, so $\partial_\nu t<0$. This contradicts the nonnegative derivative into $\Omega_R$ at a boundary minimum.

Consider an interior contact. Let $E_n=C(1+n)^N[\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}+v(\rho_0+\rho_1)]$ denote the error in <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower">[n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower]</a>. Because $\rho_0$ has a positive minimum on $\mathcal K$, $\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}\le C_{\mathcal K}\rho_0$. Also $v\rho_0\le\rho_0$, and $\rho/\rho_0$ is globally bounded. We can therefore choose a polynomial $C_n$ so large that, pointwise for all $0\le v\le1$, <a id="n3:deformation:penalty-choice"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:penalty-choice}
 \mathcal P\ge E_n+2\rho+\rho_0.$$ At the floor $m_0=1$, so the scalar equation and the lower estimate give $$\begin{split}
 0
 &\ge \delta_0\mathcal T+(1-\delta_0)\tau a\sigma
                     +\mathcal P-E_n-\rho\\
 &\ge \rho+\rho_0>0,
 \end{split}$$ a contradiction. Enlarging $C_n$ below preserves this inequality and preserves its polynomial dependence.

In the last stage $f=0$, $t=Z$, $u=L$, and $v=0$. At an interior minimum, $\mathcal T=(|K|^2+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K)^2)/2$. Increase $C_n$ polynomially if necessary so that $\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho-C_n\rho_0<0$ at all such points. For $\eta_s>0$, the scalar equation at a floor minimum has left side $4L\Delta t\ge0$ and strictly negative right side. At an inner floor minimum its flux is $4\partial_\nu t=\eta_s(-H-N_B)<0$, also impossible. If $\eta_s=0$, multiplication of $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(4L(t)\nabla t)=0$ by $t$, with zero outer value and zero inner flux, gives $t=0$. Thus the last stage has no floor contact either. ◻

</details>

We have excluded floor contact for every smooth admissible solution along the specified homotopy. Section <a href="#n3:apriori:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:section">5</a> supplies the remaining a priori bounds, and Section 6 proves existence. The choice of $\mathcal P$ uses only polynomial losses in $n$; it is independent of all fixed-$n$ Schauder constants.

<a id="pm-h-30"></a>
##### A priori estimates for the deformation

We bound the height, boundary slopes, and conformal variable before using classical regularity. Fix the prepared exterior of Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">19</a>, its thresholds and collars, and $\epsilon>0$. We use the variables and four stages of Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">23</a>. A solution is smooth on a finite truncation and satisfies $t\ge-\epsilon$, so the estimates include putative floor-contact solutions. No Hessian bound or upper bound for $Z$ is assumed.

<a id="n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons"></a>
A quantity denoted by $\Pi_n$ is bounded by $C(1+n)^N$, with $C,N$ independent of the truncation, the homotopy parameter, and $n$. It can increase at successive uses. The fixed data, collars, and $\epsilon$ can enter $C,N$. A constant denoted by $C(n)$ can depend arbitrarily on these fixed data and on $n,\ell,\tau$; it is still independent of the truncation and the homotopy parameter. Constants explicitly described as fixed do not depend on $n$. Recall that $$\ell=e^{-\epsilon n},\qquad \tau=\ell^{3/2},\qquad
 \ell\le l\le e,\qquad 0\le p\le n,
 \qquad \frac{4d}{4+n}\le\chi\le d.
 \label{n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons}$$ In particular $\Pi_n\tau/\ell\to0$. This small factor will absorb only terms whose constants are polynomial.

<a id="pm-h-31"></a>
###### Sublevels and exclusion of boundary layers

For notation in this section, let $\mathcal B_c$ be the full closed maximal black region at threshold $c$, and let $\mathcal W_c$ be the corresponding white region with $\mathcal B_{c_b}$ held fixed. These are the families used in Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">19</a>.

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:sublevels" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:apriori:lower-height"></a>
**Lemma 29** (Uniform separation from the wrong height). *In the first two homotopy stages, the following holds. If $Q\subset\bar\Omega$ is compact and disjoint from $\mathcal B_{c_b}$, there are $\eta_Q>0$ and $n_Q$ such that $$h\ge b_-+\eta_Q\quad\hbox{on }Q
 \label{n3:apriori:lower-height}$$ for every $n\ge n_Q$, every sufficiently large allowed truncation, and every admissible or floor-contact solution in those stages. If $Q$ is disjoint from $\mathcal W_{c_w}$, the analogous conclusion is $h\le b_+-\eta_Q$. The compact sets are relative to the full closure: they may contain faces of the opposite color.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels</summary>

*Proof.* We prove the lower assertion. It is enough to consider an arbitrary sequence $n_i\to\infty$, $R_i\to\infty$ and solutions in either of the first two stages. The elementary height and end estimates in Lemmas <a href="#n3:deformation:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:height">24</a> and <a href="#n3:deformation:end-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:end-height">25</a> give <a id="n3:apriori:elementary-height"></a>$$|h_i|\le C_0,\qquad
 |h_i|\le C(r^{-\gamma}-R_i^{-\gamma})\quad\hbox{on the end},
 \qquad 3/4<\gamma<1.
 \label{n3:apriori:elementary-height}$$ Near each white face extend $h_i$ to the other side by the constant $b_+$. Extend the fixed geometric coefficients smoothly there. The extended functions are continuous. Define the lower relaxed limit $$\underline h(x)=\lim_{j\to\infty}
       \inf\{h_i(y):i\ge j,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,y)<1/j\}.$$ It is lower semicontinuous, bounded, and satisfies the limiting end bound. No equicontinuity of $h_i$ is asserted.

Choose $b_-<k'<\min\{0,b_-+\eta\}$, where $\eta$ is the low-height sign range of the added term $D_0$. Suppose that a smooth function $\phi$ touches $\underline h$ from below at $x$, with $\underline h(x)\le k'$ and $d\phi(x)\ne0$. Exclude for the moment the black faces. Subtracting a small fourth-order localization term from $\phi$ makes the contact strict without changing its two-jet. Minimization on a small closed ball then produces points $x_i\to x$ and constants $c_i\to0$ such that $\phi+c_i$ touches $h_i$ from below at $x_i$, and $h_i(x_i)\to\underline h(x)$. The boundary of this ball cannot contain $x_i$ by strictness. Nor can $x_i$ lie on a white face or on the extended side: their values there are $b_+>k'$. Thus every sufficiently large $i$ uses the interior trace equation.

<a id="n3:apriori:relaxed-test"></a>
At these contacts, $$\nabla f_i=\tau_i^{-1}\nabla\phi,
 \qquad
 d_i\le\frac{\tau_i^2}{\ell_i^2|d\phi(x_i)|^2}
          \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad a_i\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad \chi_i\longrightarrow0.$$ Here $a_i=l_i|\nabla f_i|/\sqrt{D_i}$ is the deformation variable. Positivity of $A_{\chi_i}$ and the Hessian inequality at a lower contact imply $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_{\chi_i}}K+
 \frac{l_i}{\tau_i\sqrt{D_i}}
                 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_{\chi_i}}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi
 \le F_i(x_i).$$ In the second stage $D_0\le0$ at these values; in the first stage it is absent. Consequently $\limsup F_i(x_i)\le k'+C_b$. Passing to the limit gives $$\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(d\phi)^\perp}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi}{|d\phi|}
           +\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(d\phi)^\perp}K\le k'+C_b.
 \label{n3:apriori:relaxed-test}$$ This is the expansion of the level surface of $\phi$, oriented toward increasing $\phi$. The only Hessian used in this passage is the fixed test Hessian. Removing the localization proves the assertion for non-strict contacts as well.

We now transfer the test inequality to a closed sublevel set. Fix $b_-<k<k'$ and put $E_k=\{\underline h\le k\}$. Set <a id="n3:apriori:sigmoid"></a>$$\psi_j(s)=\frac{1}{1+\exp[-j^2(s-k-j^{-1})]},
 \qquad v_j=\psi_j(\underline h).
 \label{n3:apriori:sigmoid}$$ The lower relaxed limit of $v_j$ is the function $v$ which equals zero on $E_k$ and one on its complement. Indeed, at a point of $E_k$ the fixed-point values $\psi_j(\underline h(x))$ tend to zero. If $\underline h(x)>k$, lower semicontinuity supplies a neighborhood where $\underline h>k+\delta$ for some $\delta>0$, and $v_j$ tends uniformly to one there.

Let $\varphi$ be a nonzero-gradient lower test of $v$ at a zero value. The same strict-contact localization gives lower tests $\varphi+c_j$ of $v_j$ at $y_j\to x$, with $v_j(y_j)\to0$. Since $\psi_j(k')\to1$, one has $\underline h(y_j)<k'$ eventually. Locally about $y_j$, the test value is in $(0,1)$, so $\psi_j^{-1}(\varphi+c_j)$ is a smooth lower test of $\underline h$. An increasing change of defining function does not change its oriented level expansion: if $\theta'>0$, then $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}(\theta\circ\varphi)
 =\theta'\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\varphi+\theta''d\varphi\otimes d\varphi,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(d\varphi)^\perp}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}(\theta\circ\varphi)}
 {|d(\theta\circ\varphi)|}
 =\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(d\varphi)^\perp}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\varphi}{|d\varphi|}.$$ Equation <a href="#n3:apriori:relaxed-test" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:relaxed-test">[n3:apriori:relaxed-test]</a> therefore holds for the test $\varphi+c_j$ and passes to $\varphi$. A smooth exterior support of $E_k$, with defining function negative on the containing inner side, is a lower test of $v$: shrink its neighborhood so that its positive values are less than one. Thus every such support has expansion at most $k'+C_b$.

This argument also rules out a hidden layer at a white face. The reversed white face is an exterior support of $E_k\cap\bar\Omega$ at any contact there, with expansion $$-H_B+P_B=-c_w>0.$$ For $k'$ sufficiently close to $b_-$, this is strictly greater than $k'+C_b$. The high extension ensured that all preceding low-value tests came from the interior equation, so the support contradiction applies at the face itself. Hence $E_k$ avoids every white face. The end estimate makes $E_k$ compact.

Adjoin the entire closed region $\mathcal B_{c_b}$ and fill bounded complementary pockets. At a point on its smooth black frontier, every exterior support of the union also contains the black region locally. The tangency comparison therefore bounds its expansion by $c_b<k'+C_b$. At all other frontier points the preceding sublevel argument applies. Filling pockets only removes frontier pieces and preserves this property. The resulting compact closed filled set contains the required original inner barrier with a collar, because the black region already does. It avoids the outer barriers. Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:weak-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:weak-support">18</a> places it in a smooth black trapped region at any threshold $c''>k'+C_b$ sufficiently close to $c_b$. It is consequently contained in $\mathcal B_{c''}$.

Finally let $Q$ be as in the lemma. Hausdorff right continuity at $c_b$ gives a $\delta>0$ such that $\mathcal B_{c_b+\delta}\cap Q=\varnothing$; decrease $\delta$ so that the enlarged threshold is still negative and all barriers remain strict. Choose $k,k',c''$ with $$b_-<k<k',\qquad k'+C_b<c''<c_b+\delta.$$ The construction implies $E_k\cap Q=\varnothing$ for every sequence under consideration. If the uniform estimate $h>k$ on $Q$ failed, choose violating solutions with $n_i\to\infty$, $R_i\to\infty$ and $x_i\in Q$, $h_i(x_i)\le k$. A subsequence has $x_i\to x\in Q$ and $\underline h(x)\le k$, a contradiction. This gives <a href="#n3:apriori:lower-height" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:lower-height">[n3:apriori:lower-height]</a>, after decreasing its positive margin.

For the upper assertion apply the entire argument to $(-h,-K,-C)$, interchanging colors. The reversed black faces have strictly positive white expansion $-c_b$. Their exclusion and compactness give positive distance from the black region before applying the white version of Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:weak-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:weak-support">18</a>. Adjoining the full white region is therefore legitimate in the fixed black complement. Empty white regions and missing face types cause no change: only an actually nonempty sublevel would supply a trapped seed and hence a contradiction. ◻

</details>

For the truncation quantifier, start with any $R_{\min}(n)\to\infty$ that satisfies the outer estimates of Section <a href="#n3:deformation:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:section">4</a>, and enlarge it when necessary. Failure of any asserted estimate for arbitrarily large $n$ and $R\ge R_{\min}(n)$ supplies exactly the sequence excluded above. Only finitely many compact sets will be needed below, so their thresholds can be chosen simultaneously.

<a id="pm-h-32"></a>
###### Signed collar barriers

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-collars"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:collars" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:apriori:signed-slopes"></a>
**Lemma 30** (Boundary slopes). *There are fixed constants $c,C_*>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$ and the allowed truncations, the first two stages satisfy $$\begin{array}{ll}
 c/\tau\le\partial_\nu f\le C_*/\tau&\text{on black faces},\\[2pt]
 c/\tau\le-\partial_\nu f\le C_*/\tau&\text{on white faces}.
 \end{array}
 \label{n3:apriori:signed-slopes}$$ During the third stage one still has $|\partial_\nu f|\le C_*/\tau$. On every fixed compact region needed for the final scalar-curvature estimate, the first two stages satisfy $b_-\le h\le b_+$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-collars"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-collars</summary>

<a id="n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy"></a>
*Proof.* Write $s$ for the smooth leaf parameter in an outward collar and $N=\nabla s/|ds|$. All geometric coefficients of this fixed collar are bounded, with $|ds|$ bounded above and below. At a comparison contact with $h_0=b_-+\psi(s)$, $\psi'>0$, the shared gradient gives $$d\le C\frac{\tau^2}{\ell^2(\psi')^2},\qquad
 1-a\le d,\qquad n\chi\ge c_1d\quad(n\ge4).
 \label{n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy}$$ If the slopes are in a fixed positive interval, the first bound is $d\le C\ell$. None of these comparisons uses an upper bound for $Z$.

<a id="n3:apriori:collar-trace"></a>
The trace operator on this test is $$\begin{aligned}
 &\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}\left(K+
       \frac{l}{\tau\sqrt D}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}h_0\right)\notag\\
 &\quad=P_s+aH_s+\chi K(N,N)
       +a\chi\left(
           \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}s(N,N)}{|ds|}
                      +|ds|\frac{\psi''}{\psi'}\right),
 \label{n3:apriori:collar-trace}
\end{aligned}$$ where $P_s$ is the tangential trace of $K$ on the leaf. Thus it is the leaf expansion $H_s+P_s$, with an error of absolute value at most $C d$, plus the displayed logarithmic-slope term. The same formula for a negative slope has $a$ replaced by $-a$ in the Hessian terms. This is an evaluation at the contact variables; it does not differentiate the unknown $t$.

<a id="n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual"></a>
On a black collar $H_s+P_s\ge c_b$ and $C=C_b-k_Bs$. Choose small positive slopes so that $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(s)\le k_Bs/2$. At the outer end of a sufficiently short fixed collar, Lemma <a href="#n3:apriori:sublevels" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:sublevels">29</a> lets this test lie below the solution. In the compatible direction the add-on $D_0$ vanishes. The residual of the trace equation on the test is therefore at least $$k_Bs/2-Cd+a\chi|ds|\frac{\psi''}{\psi'}.
 \label{n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual}$$ Choose a smooth nonnegative $\beta_n(s)$ equal to $An$ for $0\le s\le1/n$, supported in $0\le s\le2/n$, and satisfying $\int\beta_n\le2A$. Define $$\psi'(s)=m\exp\left(\int_0^s\beta_n(q)\,\mathrm dq\right).$$ Choose the fixed $A$ large enough that the final term of <a href="#n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual">[n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual]</a> dominates $Cd$ on $s\le1/n$, using <a href="#n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy">[n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy]</a> and $a\ge1/2$ there. On $s\ge1/n$, the first term dominates $Cd\le C\ell$ for large $n$; the taper contributes with the good sign. Since the slope multiplier is at most $e^{2A}$, a fixed sufficiently small $m>0$ enforces all the previous small-slope requirements. This constructs a strict lower barrier with slopes bounded above and below independently of $n$.

An upper barrier from $b_-$ is constructed in the same collar with $$\psi'(s)=M\exp\left(-\int_0^s\beta_n(q)\,\mathrm dq\right).$$ The smooth leaf expansion differs from its boundary value by $O(s)$.
